sentences.zh: 張寧，字靖之，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ning, courtesy name Jingzhi, was a man of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ning, whose courtesy name was Jingzhi, came from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as a supervising secretary in the Rites Section of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，帝從唐瑜等奏，考核南京大小諸臣。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year, the emperor followed the memorial of Tang Yu and others and conducted performance reviews of great and small officials at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year, the emperor accepted the memorial of Tang Yu and others and ordered performance reviews of all officials, great and small, at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 寧言：「京師尤根本地，不可獨免。」

translations.literal: Ning said: "The capital is above all the root foundation of the realm and cannot alone be exempt."
translations.idiomatic: Ning argued: "The capital is the very foundation of the state and ought not to be exempted on its own."

sentences.zh: 又言：「京衛帶俸武職，一衛至二千余人，通計三萬余員。

translations.literal: He also said: "Military posts in the capital guards drawing salaries number more than two thousand in a single guard, totaling more than thirty thousand men in all.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Salaried military posts in the capital guards run to more than two thousand men per guard—more than thirty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 歲需銀四十八萬，米三十六萬，並他折俸物，動經百萬。

translations.literal: Each year they require four hundred eighty thousand taels of silver and three hundred sixty thousand piculs of grain, and with other salary substitutes the outlay routinely exceeds one million.
translations.idiomatic: Each year they consume four hundred eighty thousand taels of silver and three hundred sixty thousand piculs of grain; with other salary substitutes in kind, the cost routinely exceeds one million.

sentences.zh: 耗損國儲，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: Nothing drains the national stores more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing depletes the national treasury more severely.

sentences.zh: 而其間多老弱不嫻騎射之人。

translations.literal: Among them are many who are old, weak, and unskilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Many of them are old or weak and unskilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 莫若簡可者，補天下都司、衛所缺官，而悉汰其余。」

translations.literal: Better to select those who are fit, fill vacant posts in the realm's regional commands and guards, and dismiss all the rest."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to select the able, assign them to fill vacancies in regional commands and guards throughout the empire, and dismiss all the rest."

sentences.zh: 議格不行。

translations.literal: The proposal was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was blocked and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 帝得疾，適遇星變，詔罷明年元會，百官朝參如朔望。

translations.literal: The emperor fell ill; it happened to coincide with a celestial anomaly, and an edict canceled the New Year's assembly for the coming year, ordering officials to attend court on the first and fifteenth as at new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, a celestial anomaly occurred at the same time, and he ordered the New Year's court assembly canceled for the following year, directing officials to attend court only on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 寧言：「四方來覲，不得一睹天顏，疑似之際，必至訛言相驚，願勉循舊典，用慰人心。」

translations.literal: Ning said: "Envoys from the four quarters come to court and cannot glimpse the imperial countenance; at a time of suspicion this will surely breed alarming rumors—I beg Your Majesty to strive to follow the old precedent and thereby reassure hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Ning urged: "Tributaries from every quarter have come to court and cannot even glimpse the Son of Heaven; in such a moment of uncertainty, alarming rumors are sure to spread. I beg Your Majesty to adhere to the established precedent and thereby reassure the people."

sentences.zh: 帝疾不能從，而「奪門」之變作。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness prevented compliance, and the "Gate Seizure" coup followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was too ill to comply, and soon afterward came the "Gate Seizure" coup.

sentences.zh: 天順中，曹、石竊柄。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun era, Cao and Shi usurped power.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign, Cao Qin and Shi Heng seized power.

sentences.zh: 事關禮科者，寧輒裁損，英宗以是知寧。

translations.literal: Whenever matters concerned the Rites Section, Ning would cut them down, and Yingzong came to know Ning for this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a matter fell within the Rites Section's purview, Ning would pare it back, and for this Yingzong came to know his worth.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮與鄰部毛憐衛仇殺，詔寧同都指揮武忠往解。

translations.literal: Korea and the neighboring Maolian Guard were locked in a feud of mutual killing; the emperor ordered Ning to go with Regional Commander Wu Zhong to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: Korea and the neighboring Maolian Guard were locked in a blood feud; the emperor ordered Ning to accompany Regional Commander Wu Zhong to settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 寧辭義慷慨，而忠驍健，張兩弓折之，射雁一發墜，朝鮮人大驚服，兩人竟解其仇而還。

translations.literal: Ning's words were lofty and impassioned, while Zhong was fierce and strong—he drew two bows and broke them, shot a wild goose and brought it down with one arrow; the Koreans were greatly awed and submitted, and the two men at last settled the feud and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ning spoke with eloquent moral force, while Zhong was a formidable warrior who drew two bows at once and snapped them, then brought down a wild goose with a single shot. The Koreans were deeply impressed, and the two envoys succeeded in ending the feud before returning home.

sentences.zh: 中官覃包邀與相見，不往。

translations.literal: The eunuch Tan Bao invited him to meet and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tan Bao invited him to an audience, but he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 尋擢都給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初禦經筵，請日以《大學衍義》進講。

translations.literal: When Xianzong first attended the Classics Lecture, Ning asked that the Expanded Meaning of the Great Learning be lectured daily.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong first took his seat at the Classics Lecture, Ning requested that the Expanded Meaning of the Great Learning be read and explained to him every day.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，皇太后生辰，禮部尚書姚夔仍故事，設齋建醮，會百官赴壇行香。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, on the empress dowager's birthday, Minister of Rites Yao Kui followed precedent, set out a vegetarian feast and established a Daoist rite, and gathered officials to go to the altar and burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: That October, on the empress dowager's birthday, Minister of Rites Yao Kui followed precedent by arranging a vegetarian feast and a Daoist ritual, summoning the officials to the altar to burn incense.

sentences.zh: 寧言無益，徒傷大體，乞禁止。

translations.literal: Ning said it was of no benefit and only harmed the great propriety, and begged that it be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Ning argued that the practice was useless and damaged the dignity of the court, and he asked that it be banned.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，給事中王徽以牛玉事劾大學士李賢，得罪。

translations.literal: Before long, Supervising Secretary Wang Hui impeached Grand Secretary Li Xian over the Niu Yu affair and was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Supervising Secretary Wang Hui impeached Grand Secretary Li Xian over the Niu Yu affair and was punished for it.

sentences.zh: 寧率六科論救，由是浸與內閣忤。

translations.literal: Ning led the six sections in memorials to save him, and from this gradually fell out with the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ning led the six censorial sections in memorials on Wang's behalf, and from that time he increasingly clashed with the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會王竑等薦寧堪僉都御史清軍職貼黃，與嶽正並舉。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Hong and others recommended Ning as fit for vice censor-in-chief to purge military posts and review yellow registers, naming him together with Yue Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: About then Wang Hong and others recommended Ning as qualified to serve as vice censor-in-chief charged with purging military posts and reviewing yellow registers, naming him together with Yue Zheng.

sentences.zh: 得旨，會舉多私，皆予外任。

translations.literal: An edict came down: since the recommendations were largely private favoritism, all were given posts outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the recommendations had been largely motivated by private favoritism and ordered all those named to provincial appointments.

sentences.zh: 寧出為汀州知府，以簡靜為治，期年善政具舉。

translations.literal: Ning went out as prefect of Tingzhou, governing with simplicity and calm, and within a year every good policy was in place.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was sent out as prefect of Tingzhou, where he governed with restraint and calm; within a year his administration was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 寧才高負誌節，善章奏，聲稱籍甚。

translations.literal: Ning's talent was high and he bore lofty resolve; he excelled at memorials, and his reputation was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was highly gifted and principled, skilled at memorial writing, and enjoyed a towering reputation.

sentences.zh: 英宗嘗欲重用之，不果。

translations.literal: Yingzong once wished to employ him heavily, but it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong had once wished to give him greater responsibility, but the opportunity never came.

sentences.zh: 久居諫垣，不為大臣所喜。

translations.literal: He long dwelt in the remonstrance posts and was not liked by great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He had long served in the remonstrance offices and was disliked by the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 既出守，益郁郁不得誌，以病免歸。

translations.literal: Once sent out to guard a prefecture, he grew ever more depressed at failing to realize his aims and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After his provincial appointment, he grew increasingly frustrated at being unable to fulfill his ambitions and eventually retired home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 家居三十年，言者屢薦，終不復召。

translations.literal: He lived at home for thirty years; remonstrators repeatedly recommended him, but he was never summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for thirty years; censors repeatedly recommended him, but he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 有二妾。

translations.literal: He had two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He had two concubines.

sentences.zh: 寧沒，剪發誓死，樓居不下者四十年。

translations.literal: When Ning died, they cut their hair and vowed to die, dwelling in upper chambers and not coming down for forty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning died, they cut their hair and vowed to follow him in death, living in an upper chamber and refusing to come down for forty years.

sentences.zh: 詔旌為「雙節」。

translations.literal: An edict commended them as "Double Chastity."
translations.idiomatic: The court honored them with the title "Double Chastity."

sentences.zh: 王徽，字尚文，應天人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, styled Shangwen, native of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, styled Shangwen, was a native of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 天順四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourth year of Tianshun (1460).

sentences.zh: 除南京刑科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed supervising secretary of the Nanjing Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Nanjing Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位數月，與同官王淵、朱寬、李翔、李鈞疏陳四事。

translations.literal: Several months after Xianzong took the throne, together with his colleagues Wang Yuan, Zhu Kuan, Li Xiang, and Li Jun he submitted a memorial setting forth four matters.
translations.idiomatic: Several months after Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he and his colleagues Wang Yuan, Zhu Kuan, Li Xiang, and Li Jun submitted a memorial setting forth four matters.

sentences.zh: 末言：「自古宦官賢良者少，奸邪者多。

translations.literal: At the end they said: "Since antiquity few eunuchs have been worthy and good, while many have been wicked and depraved.
translations.idiomatic: At the end they said: "Since antiquity few eunuchs have been worthy and good, while many have been wicked and depraved.

sentences.zh: 若授以大權，致令敗壞，然後加刑，是始愛而終殺之，非所以保全之也。

translations.literal: If great power is granted them, causing ruin, and punishment is applied only afterward, that is to love them at first and kill them in the end—it is not the way to preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: If great power is granted them and ruin follows, punishment applied only afterward is to love them at first and destroy them in the end—it is not the way to preserve them.

sentences.zh: 願法高皇帝舊制，毋令預政典兵，置產立業。

translations.literal: We beg that Your Majesty follow the old institutions of the August Founder and not allow them to participate in government or command troops, establish estates, or build up enterprises.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Your Majesty follow the old institutions of the dynastic founder and not allow them to participate in government or command troops, establish estates, or build up enterprises.

sentences.zh: 家人義子，悉編原籍為民。

translations.literal: Household members and adopted sons should all be registered in their original domiciles as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Household members and adopted sons should all be registered in their original domiciles as commoners.

sentences.zh: 嚴禁官吏與之交接。

translations.literal: Officials should be strictly forbidden to associate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should be strictly forbidden to associate with them.

sentences.zh: 惟厚其賞賚，使得豐足，無復他望。

translations.literal: Only enrich their rewards and grants so that they may be abundantly provided and have no further desires.
translations.idiomatic: Only enrich their rewards and grants so that they may live in comfort and desire nothing more.

sentences.zh: 此國家之福，亦宦官之福也。」

translations.literal: This is a blessing to the state and also a blessing to the eunuchs themselves."
translations.idiomatic: This would be a blessing to the state and also a blessing to the eunuchs themselves."

sentences.zh: 其冬，帝入萬妃譖，廢吳後，罪中官牛玉擅易中宮，謫之南京，徽復與淵等劾之曰：陛下冊立中宮，此何等事，而賊臣牛玉乃大肆奸欺！

translations.literal: That winter the emperor accepted the slander of Consort Wan, deposed Empress Wu, and charged the eunuch Niu Yu with unlawfully changing the empress—banishing him to Nanjing; Hui again joined Yuan and others in impeaching him, saying: "Your Majesty's investiture of the empress—what sort of affair is this, that the traitor minister Niu Yu should commit great fraud!"
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor heeded the slanders of Lady Wan, deposed Empress Wu, and charged the eunuch Niu Yu with unlawfully replacing the empress, banishing him to Nanjing. Wang Hui again joined Wang Yuan and others in impeaching him, saying: "Your Majesty's investiture of an empress is a matter of the utmost gravity—yet the traitorous minister Niu Yu perpetrated gross deception!"

sentences.zh: 中宮既退，人情鹹謂玉必萬死。

translations.literal: Once the empress was removed, popular sentiment all said Yu must die ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress had been removed, everyone expected Niu Yu to face execution.

sentences.zh: 顧僅斥陪京，猶全首領，則凡侍陛下左右者將何所忌憚哉？

translations.literal: Yet he was only banished to the auxiliary capital and still kept his head—then what will those who attend Your Majesty's side have to fear or respect?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was merely banished to the auxiliary capital and kept his life—what restraint will those who serve at Your Majesty's side feel thereafter?

sentences.zh: 內閣大臣，身居輔弼，視立後大事漠然不以加意。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat ministers, occupying the role of assistants, looked on the great matter of establishing an heir with indifference and gave it no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat ministers, who serve as the emperor's chief advisers, treated the momentous question of establishing an heir with utter indifference.

sentences.zh: 方玉欺肆之初，婚禮未成，禮官畏權，輒為阿附。

translations.literal: At the outset of Yu's arrogant fraud, before the marriage rites were complete, the ritual officials feared power and readily flattered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Yu first began his deceit, before the marriage rites were even completed, the ritual officials, fearing his power, simply flattered him.

sentences.zh: 及玉事發之後，國法難貸，刑官念舊，竟至茍容。

translations.literal: After Yu's affair came to light, national law could hardly pardon him, yet the penal officials, mindful of old ties, ended by tolerating him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: After the affair was exposed, the law could hardly spare him, yet the penal officials, remembering old ties, let him off lightly.

sentences.zh: 而李賢等又坐視成敗，不出一言。

translations.literal: Li Xian and the others again sat by watching success or failure and uttered not a word.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and his colleagues simply watched events unfold without raising a word of protest.

sentences.zh: 黨惡欺君，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: To shield the wicked and deceive the ruler—nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Shielding the wicked and deceiving the sovereign—nothing could be worse.

sentences.zh: 請並罪賢等，為大臣不忠者戒。

translations.literal: We beg that Xian and the others be punished together, as a warning to disloyal great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Li Xian and the others be punished as well, to warn ministers who fail in their duty.

sentences.zh: 臣等前疏請保全宦官，正欲防患於未萌。

translations.literal: In our earlier memorial we asked to preserve the eunuchs—precisely intending to guard against trouble before it sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: In our earlier memorial we urged restraint toward the eunuchs precisely in order to prevent trouble before it arose.

sentences.zh: 乃處置之道未聞，牛玉之禍果作。

translations.literal: Yet no policy of handling them was heard, and the disaster of Niu Yu indeed came about.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no corrective policy was adopted, and the disaster of Niu Yu duly followed.

sentences.zh: 然往不可諫，來猶可追。

translations.literal: What is past cannot be admonished, but what is to come may still be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be undone, but the future may still be set right.

sentences.zh: 臣等不敢遠引，請以近事征之。

translations.literal: We dare not cite distant examples; we beg to take recent events as proof.
translations.idiomatic: We need not reach far back in history; recent events are proof enough.

sentences.zh: 正統末，有王振矣，詎意復有曹吉祥。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong there was Wang Zhen—who would have thought there would again be Cao Jixiang?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhengtong reign there was Wang Zhen—who could have imagined that Cao Jixiang would follow?

sentences.zh: 天順初，有吉祥矣，詎意復有牛玉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun there was Jixiang—who would have thought there would again be Niu Yu?
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianshun there was Cao Jixiang—who could have imagined that Niu Yu would appear in turn?

sentences.zh: 若又不思預防，安知後不有甚於牛玉者哉？

translations.literal: If again there is no thought of prevention, how can we know that later there will not be one worse than Niu Yu?
translations.idiomatic: If no preventive measures are taken now, who can say that someone worse than Niu Yu will not arise later?

sentences.zh: 夫宦者無事之時似乎恭慎，一聞國政，即肆奸欺。

translations.literal: Eunuchs in times of no business seem respectful and cautious; once they hear of state affairs, they at once commit wanton fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs seem respectful and cautious when they have nothing to do; the moment they hear of state affairs, they commit brazen fraud.

sentences.zh: 將用某人也，必先賣之以為己功；

translations.literal: When someone is to be employed, they first sell the appointment to claim credit for themselves;
translations.idiomatic: When someone is to be appointed, they first trade on the appointment to claim credit for themselves;

sentences.zh: 將行某事也，必先泄之以張己勢。

translations.literal: when some affair is to be carried out, they first leak it to expand their own power.
translations.idiomatic: when some policy is to be enacted, they first leak it to magnify their own influence.

sentences.zh: 迨趨附日眾，威權日盛，而禍作矣。

translations.literal: When flatterers grow daily numerous and authority daily flourishes, disaster then arises.
translations.idiomatic: As followers multiply day by day and their power grows, calamity is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 此所以不可預聞國政也。

translations.literal: This is why they must not be allowed to hear state affairs in advance.
translations.idiomatic: This is why they must not be allowed advance knowledge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 內官在帝左右，大臣不識廉恥，多與交結。

translations.literal: With inner officials at the emperor's side, great ministers who know no shame mostly associate with them.
translations.idiomatic: With eunuchs at the emperor's side, ministers who lack any sense of shame commonly cultivate ties with them.

sentences.zh: 饋獻珍奇，伊優取媚，即以為賢，而朝夕譽之。

translations.literal: They present rare treasures, fawn and curry favor, and are taken for worthy men and praised morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: They send rare gifts, fawn and flatter, and are hailed as worthy men and praised to the emperor day and night.

sentences.zh: 有方正不阿者，即以為不肖，而朝夕讒謗之，日加浸潤，未免致疑。

translations.literal: Those who are upright and unyielding are taken for unworthy, slandered morning and evening, daily steeped in insinuation, until suspicion cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are upright and unbending are branded unworthy and slandered day and night; drip by drip the emperor's suspicion is aroused.

sentences.zh: 由是稱譽者獲顯，讒謗者被斥。

translations.literal: Thus those praised gain advancement, and those slandered are driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who are praised rise, and those who are slandered are driven out.

sentences.zh: 恩出於內侍，怨歸於朝廷，此所以不可許其交結也。

translations.literal: Favor issues from inner attendants, resentment falls on the court—this is why their association must not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Favor flows from the eunuchs while resentment falls on the court—this is why such associations must be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 內官弟侄授職任事，倚勢為非，聚奸養惡。

translations.literal: Junior kinsmen of inner officials receive appointments and hold office, relying on power to do wrong, gathering villains and nurturing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Nephews and younger relatives of eunuchs are given offices and rely on their patrons' power to do wrong, gathering villains and nurturing corruption.

sentences.zh: 廣營財利，奸弊多端。

translations.literal: They broadly pursue profit, with many kinds of fraud and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: They pursue profit on every side, and their abuses are legion.

sentences.zh: 身雖居內，心實在外。

translations.literal: Though their bodies dwell within, their hearts are truly outside.
translations.idiomatic: Though they live within the palace, their interests lie entirely outside it.

sentences.zh: 內外交通，亂所由起，此所以不可使其子侄在外任職營立家產也。

translations.literal: Inner and outer communicate—rebellion arises from this; this is why their sons and nephews must not be allowed to hold office outside and build up family estates.
translations.idiomatic: When inside and outside are linked, disorder follows; this is why their sons and nephews must not be allowed to hold office outside the palace or build up family fortunes.

sentences.zh: 臣等職居言路，不為茍容，雖死無悔，惟陛下裁察。

translations.literal: We, whose office is the path of speech, will not curry favor; though we die we have no regret—only may Your Majesty judge and examine.
translations.idiomatic: We who hold the office of remonstrance will not curry favor; we would die without regret. We beg Your Majesty to weigh our words.

sentences.zh: 詔謂「妄言邀譽」，欲加罪。

translations.literal: An edict said they had "spoken falsely to win reputation" and wished to add crimes against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's reply called their words "false boasting meant to win praise" and moved to punish them further.

sentences.zh: 諸給事、御史交章論救，乃並謫州判官。

translations.literal: The various supervising secretaries and censorists submitted memorials in turn pleading for them, yet all were together demoted to prefectural assistant magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censorists filed one memorial after another in their defense, but the court still demoted them all to assistant magistrates in distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 徽得貴州普安，淵茂州，寬潼川，翔寧州，鈞綏德。

translations.literal: Hui received Pu'an in Guizhou; Yuan, Maozhou; Kuan, Tongchuan; Xiang, Ningzhou; Jun, Suide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui was sent to Pu'an in Guizhou, Wang Yuan to Maozhou, Zhu Kuan to Tongchuan, Li Xiang to Ningzhou, and Li Jun to Suide.

sentences.zh: 奏蓋鈞筆也。

translations.literal: The memorial was surely in Jun's brush.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial had almost certainly been drafted by Li Jun.

sentences.zh: 侍郎葉盛、編修陳音相繼請留，不納。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Ye Sheng and Compiler Chen Yin in succession asked that they be retained; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Ye Sheng and Compiler Chen Yin both pleaded in turn that the men be kept at court, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 最後御史楊瑯言尤切，幾得罪。

translations.literal: Finally Censor Yang Lang spoke most urgently and nearly incurred punishment himself.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Lang spoke last and most sharply of all and nearly brought punishment on himself as well.

sentences.zh: 微至普安，興學校教士，始有舉於鄉者。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Pu'an, he raised schools and taught scholars; for the first time someone from there gained recommendation in the local examinations.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Hui reached Pu'an, he founded schools and trained local scholars, and the district produced its first successful candidate in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 卻土官隴暢及白千戶賄，治甚有聲。

translations.literal: He refused bribes from the native official Long Chang and the Bai chiliarch household; his governance gained a very great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He turned away bribes from the native chieftain Long Chang and from the Bai chiliarch household, and his administration won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 居七年，棄官歸，言者屢薦，終以宦官惡之不復錄。

translations.literal: After seven years he abandoned his office and returned home; remonstrators repeatedly recommended him, but in the end, because eunuchs hated him, he was never again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years he resigned and went home. Critics at court recommended him again and again, yet the eunuchs' hostility kept him from ever being reappointed.

sentences.zh: 徽嘗曰：「今仕者以剛方為刻，怠緩為寬。

translations.literal: Hui once said: "Today officeholders take uprightness and firmness to be harshness, and slackness and delay to be leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui once remarked, "Officials today call stern integrity harshness and call laziness leniency.

sentences.zh: 學者以持正為滯，恬軟為通。

translations.literal: Scholars take holding to what is right to be stagnation, and easy softness to be penetration.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars treat moral firmness as obstinacy and treat easy compliance as sophistication.

sentences.zh: 為文以典雅為膚淺，怪異為古健。」

translations.literal: In writing they take elegance and refinement to be superficiality, and strangeness and oddity to be ancient vigor."
translations.idiomatic: In writing they dismiss elegance as shallow and praise the bizarre as true classical strength."

sentences.zh: 其論治，嘗誦張宣公語「無求辦事之人，當求曉事之人」，時皆服其切中。

translations.literal: In his discourse on governance he would recite Zhang Xuangong's words: "Do not seek men who merely get tasks done; seek men who understand affairs," and at the time all admired how penetratingly he had hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of government he often quoted Zhang Xuangong: "Do not look for men who merely get tasks done; look for men who understand affairs." His contemporaries all agreed that he had struck the truth.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，吏部尚書王恕薦起陜西左參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, Minister of Personnel Wang Su recommended him and he was raised to Left Participating Administrator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign, Minister of Personnel Wang Su had him recalled and appointed Left Participating Administrator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 逾年，謝病還，卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: After more than a year he pleaded illness and returned; he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he resigned on grounds of illness and went home, where he died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子韋，見《文苑傳》。

translations.literal: His son Wei is treated in the "Treatise on Letters and Arts."
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei is discussed in the Treatise on Letters and Arts.

sentences.zh: 王淵，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan was a man of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 天順元年進士，除南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the first year of Tianshun, he was appointed supervising secretary in the Personnel Section at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the first year of Tianshun and was made a supervising secretary in the Nanjing Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 素伉直，終順天府治中。

translations.literal: By nature upright and direct, he ended as Assistant Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally forthright and unyielding, he finished his career as assistant prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 朱寬，莆田人，李翔，大足人，皆天順元年進士。

translations.literal: Zhu Kuan was a man of Putian; Li Xiang was a man of Dazu; both were metropolitan graduates in the first year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kuan was from Putian and Li Xiang from Dazu; both had passed the metropolitan examination in the first year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 李鈞，永新人，景泰二年進士。

translations.literal: Li Jun was a man of Yongxin and a metropolitan graduate in the second year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun came from Yongxin and had passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 寬為南京禮科給事中，翔兵科，鈞工科。

translations.literal: Kuan served as supervising secretary in the Rites Section at Nanjing, Xiang in the Military Section, and Jun in the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kuan was a supervising secretary in the Nanjing Rites Section, Li Xiang in the Military Section, and Li Jun in the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 既被謫，寬進表入京，道卒。

translations.literal: After they had been demoted, Kuan submitted a memorial and entered the capital, but died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: After their demotion Zhu Kuan sent in a memorial and set out for the capital, but died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 翔、鈞皆以判官終。

translations.literal: Xiang and Jun both ended their lives as assistant magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang and Li Jun both died in exile as assistant magistrates.

sentences.zh: 毛弘，字士廣，鄞人。

translations.literal: Mao Hong, style name Shiguang, was a man of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hong, whose style was Shiguang, came from Yin.

sentences.zh: 登天順初進士。

translations.literal: He attained the status of metropolitan graduate at the beginning of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination early in the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 六年授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed supervising secretary in the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the reign he was appointed supervising secretary in the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 成化三年夏，偕六科諸臣上言：「比塞上多事，正陛下宵衣旰食時。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Chenghua, together with the various officials of the Six Sections he submitted a statement: "Of late the northern frontier has had many affairs; this is just the time when Your Majesty should rise at dawn and eat at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Chenghua he joined the officials of the Six Sections in a memorial: "The northern frontier has been troubled lately; this is precisely the moment when Your Majesty ought to be laboring from dawn until night.

sentences.zh: 乃聞退朝之暇，頗事逸遊。

translations.literal: Yet we hear that in the leisure after retiring from court Your Majesty rather pursues idle roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we hear that after court Your Majesty often devotes his leisure to pleasure outings.

sentences.zh: 炮聲數聞於外，非禁城所宜有。

translations.literal: The sound of cannon is repeatedly heard outside; this is not what the Forbidden City ought to have.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon fire is heard again and again beyond the walls, which is hardly fitting for the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 況災變頻仍，兩畿水旱，川、廣兵草之余，公私交困。

translations.literal: Moreover disasters and portents come in succession; the two capitals regions suffer flood and drought; in the wake of war in Sichuan and Guangdong, public and private alike are mutually distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters have followed one after another: both capital regions have suffered flood and drought, and Sichuan and Guangdong are still recovering from war, so state and people alike are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 願省遊戲宴飲之娛，停金豆、銀豆之賞。

translations.literal: We wish that Your Majesty would reduce the pleasure of games, banquets, and drinking, and stop the rewards of gold beans and silver beans.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to cut back on games, feasts, and drinking, and to end the distribution of gold and silver bean prizes.

sentences.zh: 日禦經筵，講求正學，庶幾上解天怒，下慰人心。」

translations.literal: Daily attend the Classics Lecture and pursue orthodox learning, so that perhaps above Heaven's anger may be eased and below the people's hearts may be comforted."
translations.idiomatic: Attend the Classics Lecture every day and devote yourself to proper learning, so that Heaven's anger may be appeased and the people's hearts reassured."

sentences.zh: 御史展毓等亦以為言，皆嘉納。

translations.literal: Censor Zhan Yu and others also spoke to the same effect, and all were praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhan Yu and others made the same plea, and the emperor praised and accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 帝從學士商輅請，改元後建言罷官者悉錄用。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Academician Shang Lu's request: after the change of reign title, all who had been dismissed for offering remonstrance were entirely reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: At Academician Shang Lu's urging, the emperor reinstated everyone who had lost office for remonstrating after the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 弘請斷自踐阼而後，召還給事中王徽等，不許。

translations.literal: Hong asked that the line be drawn from after the emperor's accession to the throne, and that Supervising Secretary Wang Hui and others be recalled; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hong asked that only dismissals after the emperor's accession be reversed and that Wang Hui and the other supervising secretaries be recalled, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 慈懿太后崩，詔別葬。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ciyi died, and an edict ordered a separate burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ciyi died, the court ordered that she be buried apart from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 弘偕魏元等疏諫，未得請。

translations.literal: Hong, together with Wei Yuan and others, submitted a memorial remonstrating, but did not obtain assent.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hong joined Wei Yuan and others in a memorial of protest, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 朝罷，弘倡言曰：「此大事，吾輩當以死諫，請合大小臣工伏闕固爭。」

translations.literal: When court was dismissed, Hong initiated speech, saying: "This is a great matter; we ought to remonstrate unto death. I ask that great and small officials together prostrate at the gate and firmly contend."
translations.idiomatic: After court Mao Hong spoke up: "This is a grave matter. We must remonstrate even at the cost of our lives. Let all officials, high and low, kneel at the palace gate and refuse to yield."

sentences.zh: 眾許諾。

translations.literal: The multitude promised assent.
translations.idiomatic: The others agreed.

sentences.zh: 有退卻者，給事中張賓呼曰：「君輩獨不受國恩乎，何為首鼠兩端。」

translations.literal: When some drew back, Supervising Secretary Zhang Bin called out: "Do you alone not receive the state's grace? Why act like a rat that looks two ways?"
translations.idiomatic: When some started to pull back, Supervising Secretary Zhang Bin shouted, "Have you alone received no favor from the state? Why waver like a timid rat?"

sentences.zh: 乃伏哭文華門，竟得如禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon they prostrated themselves and wept at the Wenhua Gate, and in the end obtained burial according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: They then knelt and wept at the Wenhua Gate until the court at last granted a burial in accordance with ritual.

sentences.zh: 弘在垣中所論列最多，聲震朝寧。

translations.literal: Among those in the Censorate quarters Hong's submitted criticisms were the most numerous, and his reputation shook court and capital.
translations.idiomatic: Within the remonstrance offices Mao Hong filed more memorials than anyone else, and his voice resounded through the court and capital.

sentences.zh: 帝頗厭苦之，嘗曰：「昨日毛弘，今日毛弘。」

translations.literal: The emperor was rather weary and vexed by this, and once said: "Yesterday Mao Hong, today Mao Hong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary of him and once remarked, "Yesterday it was Mao Hong; today it is Mao Hong again."

sentences.zh: 前後所陳，或不見聽，而弘慷慨論議無所屈。

translations.literal: What he presented before and after was sometimes not heeded, yet Hong's impassioned discourse and debate had no yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his earlier and later submissions went unheeded, yet Mao Hong continued to speak boldly and never backed down.

sentences.zh: 欽天監正谷濱受賕當除名，命輸贖貶秩。

translations.literal: Director of the Directorate of Astronomy Gu Bin, having taken bribes, ought to have been removed from the register; he was ordered to pay ransom and be demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bin, director of the Directorate of Astronomy, had taken bribes and should have been expelled, but the emperor merely ordered him to pay a fine and accept demotion.

sentences.zh: 正一真人張元吉有罪論死，詔系獄。

translations.literal: The Zhengyi Perfected Man Zhang Yuanji, guilty and sentenced to death, received an edict ordering imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji, the Zhengyi Perfected Man, had been judged guilty and condemned to death, yet an edict merely ordered him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 弘等皆固爭，終不聽。

translations.literal: Hong and the others all firmly contended, but in the end the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hong and his colleagues protested vigorously, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 三遷至都給事中。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached the post of supervising secretary-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became supervising secretary-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 得疾，暴卒。

translations.literal: He took ill and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 邱弘，字寬叔，上杭人。

translations.literal: Qiu Hong, style name Kuanshu, was a man of Shanghang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Hong, whose style was Kuanshu, came from Shanghang.

sentences.zh: 天順末進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate at the end of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination late in the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 數陳時政。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented the policies of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted critiques of current policy.

sentences.zh: 成化四年春，偕同官上言：「洪武、永樂間，以畿輔、山東土曠人稀，詔聽民開墾，永不科稅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Chenghua, together with colleagues in office he submitted a statement: "Between the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, because in the capital regions and Shandong the land was broad and the people sparse, an edict allowed the people to open wasteland for cultivation, never to be taxed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Chenghua he joined his colleagues in a memorial: "During the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, because land around the capital and in Shandong lay idle while population was thin, the throne allowed commoners to reclaim wasteland tax-free in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 邇者權豪怙勢，率指為閑田，朦朧奏乞。

translations.literal: Of late powerful families rely on influence and generally point to such land as idle fields, submitting vague petitions to beg for it.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the powerful have abused their influence, routinely calling such land "idle fields" and filing vague petitions to seize it.

sentences.zh: 如嘉善長公主求文安諸縣地，西天佛子劄實巴求靜海縣地，多至數十百頃。

translations.literal: For example, the Princess of Jiashan sought land in the counties of Wen'an and elsewhere; the Western Heaven Buddhist master Cha Shiba sought land in Jinghai County—in many cases reaching several tens or hundreds of qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiashan sought land across Wen'an and neighboring counties; the Western Heaven Buddhist master Cha Shiba sought land in Jinghai County—grants running to scores or even hundreds of qing.

sentences.zh: 夫地逾百頃，古者百家產也。

translations.literal: Now land exceeding a hundred qing was in antiquity the livelihood of a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred qing of land once supported the livelihood of a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 豈可徇一人之私情而奪百家恒產哉？」

translations.literal: How can one follow a single person's private feeling and seize the permanent livelihood of a hundred households?"
translations.idiomatic: How can the court indulge one person's private interest and strip a hundred households of their permanent livelihood?"

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，詔自今請乞，皆不許，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted their words and ordered that from now on all petitions to beg for land were not permitted, and this was written as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial and decreed that from then on all such land petitions were forbidden, and the rule was entered into statute.

sentences.zh: 劄實巴所乞地，竟還之民。

translations.literal: The land Cha Shiba had begged for was in the end returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The land Cha Shiba had sought was eventually restored to the commoners.

sentences.zh: 弘再遷，至都給事中。

translations.literal: Hong was promoted again and reached the post of supervising secretary-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Hong was promoted again and rose to supervising secretary-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，山東、河南大旱，弘請振。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, Shandong and Henan suffered great drought; Hong requested relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year a severe drought struck Shandong and Henan, and Qiu Hong asked for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 因言：「四方告災，部臣拘成例，必覆實始免。

translations.literal: He went on to say: "When the four quarters report disaster, ministry officials are bound by established precedent and must verify on investigation before exemption is granted.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Whenever disasters are reported across the realm, ministry officials cling to precedent and insist on verification before any tax relief is granted.

sentences.zh: 上雖蠲租，下鮮實惠。

translations.literal: Above, though rent is remitted, below there is little real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne may remit taxes, but the people below rarely feel the benefit.

sentences.zh: 請自今遇災，撫按官勘實，即與蠲除。」

translations.literal: We ask that from now on, whenever disaster is encountered, the grand coordinator and regional inspector investigate and verify, and remission be granted at once."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that from now on, whenever disaster strikes, the grand coordinator and regional inspector verify the facts and remit taxes immediately."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃有寵，中官梁芳、陳喜爭進淫巧；

translations.literal: Consort Wan had favor; the eunuchs Liang Fang and Chen Xi vied to present lewd ingenuity;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan held the emperor's favor, and the eunuchs Liang Fang and Chen Xi competed to offer him lewd novelties;

sentences.zh: 奸人屠宗順輩日獻奇異寶石，輒厚酬之，糜帑藏百萬計。

translations.literal: villains such as Tu Zongshun daily presented strange and rare precious stones and were at once richly rewarded, wasting treasury stores on the order of millions.
translations.idiomatic: while schemers such as Tu Zongshun daily presented exotic gems and were richly rewarded, draining the treasury by millions.

sentences.zh: 有因以得官者。

translations.literal: Some thereby obtained office.
translations.idiomatic: Some of them even won official posts through these gifts.

sentences.zh: 都人仿效，競尚侈靡，僭擬無度。

translations.literal: The people of the capital imitated them, competing to esteem extravagance, with presumptuous imitation beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital followed suit, vying in luxury and imitating court privilege without restraint.

sentences.zh: 弘偕同官疏論宗順等罪，請追還帑金，嚴禁侈俗。

translations.literal: Hong, together with colleagues in office, submitted a memorial discussing the crimes of Zongshun and others, asking that treasury gold be pursued and returned and that extravagant customs be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Hong joined his colleagues in a memorial denouncing Tu Zongshun and his like, demanding repayment to the treasury and a strict ban on extravagant customs.

sentences.zh: 事下刑部，尚書陸瑜因請置宗順等於理，沒其貲以振饑民。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Ministry of Punishments; Minister Lu Yu thereupon asked that Zongshun and others be placed before the law and their goods confiscated to relieve famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Ministry of Punishments, where Minister Lu Yu asked that Tu Zongshun and the others be prosecuted and their property seized to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，但命僭侈者罪無赦，然竟不能禁也。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit this, but only ordered that those who presumptuously practiced extravagance were to have crimes without pardon—yet in the end it could not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, merely decreeing that presumptuous extravagance would henceforth be unpardonable, yet the abuse could not be stopped after all.

sentences.zh: 京師歲歉米貴，而四方遊僧萬數，弘請驅逐，以省冗食。

translations.literal: In the capital the year was lean and rice costly, while itinerant monks from the four quarters numbered in the tens of thousands; Hong asked that they be driven away to economize on redundant consumption.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had a poor harvest and costly grain, while tens of thousands of wandering monks had gathered from all directions; Qiu Hong asked that they be expelled to cut wasteful consumption.

sentences.zh: 又請發太倉米，減價以糶，給貧民最甚者。

translations.literal: He also asked that grain from the Taicang granary be released and sold at reduced price to supply those among the poor who suffered most severely.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that grain from the Taicang granary be sold at reduced prices to the poorest of the poor.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor entirely followed these requests.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 復言：「在京百獸房及清河寺諸處，所育珍禽野獸，日飼魚肉米菽，乞並縱放，以省冗費。」

translations.literal: He spoke again: "At the Hundred Beasts Yard in the capital and at Qinghe Temple and other places, the rare birds and wild beasts that are raised are daily fed fish, meat, rice, and beans; we beg that they all be released together to economize on redundant expense."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "At the imperial menagerie, Qinghe Temple, and similar sites, rare birds and beasts are fed daily on fish, meat, rice, and grain. We beg that they all be released to cut unnecessary expense."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: A report was received in acknowledgment.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged the memorial.

sentences.zh: 明年使琉球，道卒。

translations.literal: The next year, while on mission to Ryukyu, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while en route on an embassy to Ryukyu, he died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 弘與毛弘同居言路，皆敢言，人稱「二弘」雲。

translations.literal: Hong and Mao Hong both dwelt in the path of speech and were alike daring in speech; people called them "the Two Hongs."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Hong and Mao Hong both served in the remonstrance offices and were equally outspoken; people called them "the Two Hongs."

sentences.zh: 李森，字時茂，歷城人。

translations.literal: Li Sen, style name Shimao, was a man of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sen, whose style was Shimao, came from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 天順元年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the first year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the first year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 負氣敢言。

translations.literal: He bore a spirited temperament and dared to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and outspoken by nature, he did not shrink from remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，上疏請禁朝覲官科斂征求為民害者。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor took the throne, he submitted a memorial asking that officials on court-audience duty who levied collections and exactions as harm to the people be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong Emperor ascended the throne, Li Sen memorialized to forbid officials attending court audiences from levying extractions that harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王翺請從其言，帝為下詔禁止。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Ao asked to follow his words, and the emperor thereupon issued an edict forbidding the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Ao urged acceptance of the proposal, and the emperor issued an edict banning such levies.

sentences.zh: 頃之，言：「近有無功而晉侯、伯、都督者；

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he said: "Of late there are those without merit who are advanced to marquis, earl, or regional commander;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he wrote, "Lately men without merit have been made marquises, earls, or regional commanders;

sentences.zh: 有無才德而位九列者；

translations.literal: there are those without talent or virtue who hold posts among the Nine Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: men without talent or virtue have been placed among the Nine Ministers;

sentences.zh: 有以畫、弈、彈琴、醫、卜技能而得官職者。

translations.literal: there are those who by skills in painting, go, zither-playing, medicine, and divination obtain office and position.
translations.idiomatic: and men have won office through painting, go, music, medicine, or divination alone;

sentences.zh: 名爵日輕，廩祿日費，是玩天下之公器，棄國家之大柄也。

translations.literal: Titles and ranks daily grow light, and grain salaries daily are wasted—this is to toy with the public vessels of the realm and abandon the great handles of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Titles grow cheaper by the day and salaries more costly—this treats the honors of the realm as toys and throws away the state's gravest instruments of power.

sentences.zh: 自今宜擇人授，毋令匪才競進。」

translations.literal: From now on one ought to choose men and confer office, and not allow unworthy talent to compete in advancement."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth appointments should go only to the worthy, and unfit men must not be allowed to scramble for office."

sentences.zh: 且請嚴軍官黜陟，核逃伍虛糧。

translations.literal: He also asked that military officers' dismissals and promotions be made strict and that deserters' phantom rations be audited.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for stricter discipline in promoting and demoting military officers and for an audit of deserters and fictitious ration rolls.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All received the reply "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 御史謝文祥以劾姚夔下獄，森偕同官救之，不納。

translations.literal: Censor Xie Wenxiang was imprisoned for impeaching Yao Kui; Sen, together with colleagues in office, rescued him, but this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xie Wenxiang was imprisoned for impeaching Yao Kui; Li Sen joined his colleagues in pleading for him, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，日食，瓊山縣地震，森疏陳十事。

translations.literal: The next summer there was a solar eclipse and an earthquake in Qiongshan County; Sen submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, after a solar eclipse and an earthquake in Qiongshan County, Li Sen submitted a memorial outlining ten reforms.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以貴幸侵奪民產，率諸給事言：「昔奉先帝敕，皇親強占軍民田者，罪毋赦，投獻者戍邊。

translations.literal: Before long, because favored persons seized the people's property, he led the various supervising secretaries in saying: "In former times, by command of the late emperor, where imperial kin forcibly occupied military and civilian fields, the crime was without pardon, and those who presented land were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as favored courtiers seized commoners' property, he led the supervising secretaries in a memorial: "The late emperor once decreed that any imperial relative who seized military or civilian land would be shown no mercy and that anyone who presented such land would be sent to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一時貴戚莫敢犯。

translations.literal: For a time the noble kin did not dare transgress.
translations.idiomatic: For a time even the great clans at court did not dare violate the rule.

sentences.zh: 比給事中丘弘奏絕權貴請乞，陛下亦既俯從。

translations.literal: Recently Supervising Secretary Qiu Hong memorialized to cut off the powerful and noble from begging for land, and Your Majesty also has already bowed and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Only recently Supervising Secretary Qiu Hong petitioned to end land grants to the powerful, and Your Majesty graciously agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃外戚錦衣指揮周彧求武強、武邑田六百余頃，翊聖夫人劉氏求通州、武清地三百余頃，詔皆許之，何其與前敕悖也！

translations.literal: Yet the maternal kin, Brocade-Guard Commander Zhou Yu, sought more than six hundred qing of fields in Wuqiang and Wuyi; Lady Yisheng, the Liu clan, sought more than three hundred qing of land in Tongzhou and Wuqing—and edicts permitted them all. How does this contradict the former command!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor's kin by marriage, Brocade-Guard Commander Zhou Yu, was granted more than six hundred qing in Wuqiang and Wuyi, and Lady Yisheng Liu more than three hundred qing in Tongzhou and Wuqing—and edicts approved every request. How can this be reconciled with your earlier decree?

sentences.zh: 彼溪壑難厭，而畿內膏腴有限，小民衣食皆出於此，一旦奪之，何以為生。

translations.literal: Those men are gorges and ravines hard to fill, yet within the capital regions fertile land is limited; the common people's food and clothing all come from this—once it is seized in a day, by what shall they live?
translations.idiomatic: Their greed is bottomless, yet the capital districts hold only so much rich soil; the people's food and clothing all depend on it—strip it away overnight, and how are they to survive?

sentences.zh: 且本朝百年來戶口日滋，安得尚有閑田不耕不稼？

translations.literal: Moreover, for a hundred years under this dynasty household registers have daily increased—how could there still be idle fields neither plowed nor sown?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the population has grown steadily for a century under this dynasty; how could any land still lie fallow, neither plowed nor planted?

sentences.zh: 名為奏求，實豪奪而已。」

translations.literal: The name is memorial request; in reality it is nothing but violent seizure."
translations.idiomatic: They call it a petition, but in truth it is naked expropriation."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，而已賜者仍不問。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, yet what had already been granted was still not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial, but took no action against grants already made.

sentences.zh: 山西災，山東及杭、紹、嘉、湖大水，森等請蠲振，帝並從之。

translations.literal: Shanxi suffered disaster; Shandong and Hang, Shao, Jia, and Hu were stricken by great flood—Sen and others requested tax remission and relief distribution, and the emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxi was afflicted by calamity and Shandong, Hangzhou, Shaoxing, Jiaxing, and Huzhou were ravaged by flood, Li Sen and his colleagues petitioned for tax relief and famine relief, and the emperor granted every request.

sentences.zh: 時帝未有儲嗣，而萬貴妃專寵，後宮莫得進。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had no heir apparent, while Consort Wan monopolized favor and none in the rear palace could gain access.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still had no heir, Consort Wan held his affection alone, and no other woman in the inner palace could approach him.

sentences.zh: 言者每勸上普恩澤，然未敢顯言妃妒也。

translations.literal: Those who spoke remonstrance each urged the sovereign to extend universal grace, yet did not dare openly speak of the consort's jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists repeatedly urged the emperor to extend his favor broadly, but none dared name Consort Wan's jealousy outright.

sentences.zh: 惟森抗章為言，帝心慍。

translations.literal: Only Sen submitted a forthright memorial on the matter, and the emperor's heart was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Sen spoke bluntly in a formal memorial, and the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 森已再遷左給事中，會戶科都給事中缺，吏部列森名上，詔予外任。

translations.literal: Sen had already been twice promoted to Left Supervising Secretary; it happened that the post of supervising secretary-in-chief of the Revenue Section was vacant—the Ministry of Personnel listed Sen's name and submitted it, and an edict gave him an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sen had already risen twice to Left Supervising Secretary; when the chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Section fell vacant, the Ministry of Personnel nominated him—and an edict sent him to provincial service instead.

sentences.zh: 部擬興化知府，不允，乃出為懷慶通判。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed him as prefect of Xinghua; this was not approved, and he was then sent out as vice prefect of Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended him as prefect of Xinghua, but the throne refused and appointed him vice prefect of Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，投劾歸，不復出。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted his resignation and returned home, and did not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned and retired home, never taking office again.

sentences.zh: 魏元，字景善，朝城人。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan, style name Jingshan, was a man of Chaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan, whose style was Jingshan, came from Chaocheng.

sentences.zh: 天順元年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the first year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the first year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as a supervising secretary in the Rites Section of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 成化初，萬貴妃兄弟驕橫，元疏劾之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Consort Wan's brothers were arrogant and overbearing; Yuan memorialized in impeachment of them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign, Consort Wan's brothers grew insolent and overbearing, and Wei Yuan impeached them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 四年，慈懿太后崩，將別葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Empress Dowager Ciyi died, and she was to be buried separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Empress Dowager Ciyi died, and the court planned a separate burial.

sentences.zh: 元偕同官三十九人抗章極諫，御史康永韶亦偕同官四十一人爭之，伏哭文華門，竟得如禮。

translations.literal: Yuan, together with thirty-nine colleagues in office, submitted forthright memorials remonstrating to the utmost; Censor Kang Yongshao also joined forty-one colleagues in disputing it—they prostrated themselves weeping at the Wenhua Gate, and in the end burial followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan joined thirty-nine fellow officials in fierce memorial protest; Censor Kang Yongshao and forty-one colleagues joined the struggle, weeping prostrate at the Wenhua Gate until burial was conducted according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，彗星見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: That September a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 元率諸給事上言：

translations.literal: Yuan led the various supervising secretaries in submitting words:
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan led the supervising secretaries in a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 入春以來，災異疊至，近又彗星見東方，光拂臺垣，皆陰盛陽微之證。

translations.literal: Since entering spring, disasters and anomalies have come in layers; recently again a comet has appeared in the east, its light brushing the Terrace Enclosure—all are proofs of yin flourishing and yang declining.
translations.idiomatic: Since spring, calamities have struck one after another; now a comet has risen in the east, its light sweeping the celestial observatory—signs all of yin ascendant and yang in retreat.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君之與後，猶天之與地，不可得而參貳也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the relation of ruler to heir is like heaven to earth—it cannot be made dual.
translations.idiomatic: We are taught that the bond between sovereign and heir is like that between heaven and earth; it cannot be divided in two.

sentences.zh: 傳聞宮中乃有盛寵，匹耦中宮。

translations.literal: It is reported that within the palace there is now overwhelming favor, a match for the principal palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says that within the palace one consort enjoys favor so great that she rivals the empress herself.

sentences.zh: 尚書姚夔等向嘗言之，陛下謂「內事朕自裁置」。

translations.literal: Minister Yao Kui and others formerly once spoke of this; Your Majesty said, "Inner affairs I shall arrange myself."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yao Kui and others raised this before, but Your Majesty replied, "Palace matters are for me to decide."

sentences.zh: 屏息傾聽，將及半載，而昭德宮進膳未聞少減，中宮未聞少增。

translations.literal: Holding breath and straining to listen, it will soon be half a year, yet provisions to Zhaode Palace have not been heard to diminish in the least, nor provisions to the principal palace to increase in the least.
translations.idiomatic: We have waited in silence nearly half a year, yet meals sent to Zhaode Palace have not diminished, nor have those to the empress's quarters increased.

sentences.zh: 夫宮闈雖遠，而視聽猶咫尺，衽席之微，謫見玄象，不可不懼。

translations.literal: Now though the palace gates are distant, sight and hearing are still within a foot's measure; the slightest matter of bed and mat is reproved in the dark heavens—this must be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Though the inner palace seems remote, the emperor's eyes and ears are never far away; the smallest indiscretion at the bedside is written in the heavens—this should give pause.

sentences.zh: 且陛下富有春秋，而震位尚虛。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty is rich in spring and autumn, yet the Zhen position is still empty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still in the prime of life, yet the heir's place stands vacant.

sentences.zh: 豈可以宗社大計一付之愛專情一之人，而不求所以固國本安民心哉。

translations.literal: How can the great design of altars and state be entirely entrusted to one who monopolizes affection and concentrates feeling in a single person, without seeking the means to secure the foundation of the realm and settle the people's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: How can the fate of altars and state be left to one who monopolizes your affection, without seeking to secure the succession and reassure the people?

sentences.zh: 願明伉儷之義，嚴嫡妾之防。

translations.literal: We wish that the righteousness of husband and wife be made clear and the barrier between principal wife and concubine be made strict.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to uphold the bond of marriage and enforce the distinction between wife and concubine.

sentences.zh: 俾尊卑較然，各安其分。

translations.literal: Cause high and low to be clearly compared, each resting in his or her allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Let rank be unmistakable and each person keep to her proper place.

sentences.zh: 本支百世之基，實在於此。

translations.literal: The foundation for this branch to endure a hundred generations truly lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's endurance for generations depends on this.

sentences.zh: 四方旱澇相仍，民困日棘，荊、襄流民告變。

translations.literal: In the four quarters drought and flood follow one another; the people's distress grows daily acute; in Jing and Xiang, displaced persons report disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and flood have struck in succession across the realm; the people's hardship grows daily; refugees in Jing and Xiang have risen in unrest.

sentences.zh: 陛下作民父母，初無儆惕，僅循故事，付部施行。

translations.literal: Your Majesty stands as father and mother to the people, yet at first there is no vigilance or caution—only following precedent and handing matters to the ministries for execution.
translations.idiomatic: As father and mother to the people, Your Majesty has shown little alarm, merely following routine and leaving implementation to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 而戶部尚書馬昂，凡有奏報，遇上意喜，則曰「移所司處置」；

translations.literal: Yet Minister of Revenue Ma Ang, whenever there was a memorial report, if he met the sovereign's pleasure would say, "Shift it to the responsible office for disposition";
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Ma Ang, on every memorial submitted, would say when the emperor was pleased, "Refer it to the appropriate office for action";

sentences.zh: 遇上意怒，則曰「事窒難行」；

translations.literal: if he met the sovereign's anger would say, "The matter is obstructed and hard to carry out";
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor was angry, "The matter is blocked and cannot proceed";

sentences.zh: 微有利害，即乞聖裁。

translations.literal: at the slightest benefit or harm he would immediately beg the sacred decision.
translations.idiomatic: and at the slightest difficulty he would beg the emperor's personal ruling.

sentences.zh: 首鼠依違，民更何望。

translations.literal: Like a rodent's head, wavering and irresolute—what more can the people hope for?
translations.idiomatic: Hedging and vacillating thus, what hope can the people have?

sentences.zh: 惟亟罷征稅，發內帑，遣官振贍，庶可少慰人心。

translations.literal: Only by urgently stopping levies and taxes, releasing the inner treasury, and dispatching officials to relieve and sustain might the people's hearts be somewhat comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Only by halting levies at once, opening the privy purse, and sending officials to distribute relief can the people's hearts be somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 陛下崇信異教，每遇生湣之辰，輒重糜資財，廣建齋醮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty honors and believes heterodox teachings; whenever the birth or death anniversary arrives, you then heavily waste resources and broadly build fasting rites.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has placed faith in unorthodox religions; on every birth or death anniversary you squander vast sums on elaborate fasting rituals.

sentences.zh: 而西僧劄實巴等，至加法王諸號，賜予駢蕃。

translations.literal: Moreover the Western monk Cha Shiba and others have even been given the various titles of Dharma King, with gifts bestowed in paired abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The Western monk Cha Shiba and his like have been raised to Dharma King and showered with gifts beyond count.

sentences.zh: 出乘棕輿，導用金吾仗，縉紳避道，奉養過於親王。

translations.literal: Going out they ride palanquins of palm fiber; escorts use Golden Crow guard staffs; officials in silk robes yield the road; their maintenance surpasses that of imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: They travel in palm-fiber litters, escorted by Golden Crow guards; officials scatter from their path; their upkeep exceeds that of imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 悖理亂紀，孰甚於此。

translations.literal: Against principle and disordering discipline—what exceeds this?
translations.idiomatic: Nothing more thoroughly overturns right order and ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 乞革奪名號，遣還其國，追錄橫賜，用振饑民。

translations.literal: We beg to strip their titles, send them back to their countries, recover and record their wanton grants, and use them to relieve starving people.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that their titles be revoked, that they be sent home, that their lavish gifts be recovered, and that the funds be used to succor the starving.

sentences.zh: 仍敕寺觀，永不得再講齋醮，以橐國用。

translations.literal: Further command temples and abbeys never again to conduct fasting rites, lest they drain the state's expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Further command that temples and monasteries never again hold such rites, lest they drain the treasury.

sentences.zh: 天下之財，不在官則在民。

translations.literal: The wealth of the realm, if not in the officials then is in the people.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's wealth rests either with the state or with the people.

sentences.zh: 今公私交困，由玩好太多，賞賚無節。

translations.literal: Now public and private are alike in distress, because curios and delights are too many and rewards and gifts without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Today both court and country are exhausted because indulgences are too many and rewards without limit.

sentences.zh: 或營立塔寺，或購市珍奇。

translations.literal: Some erect pagodas and temples; some purchase and market rare curiosities.
translations.idiomatic: Some funds build pagodas and temples, others buy exotic luxuries.

sentences.zh: 一物之微，累價巨萬，國帑安得不絀？

translations.literal: A single thing's slightness, piled in price to tens of thousands—how can the national treasury not be depleted?
translations.idiomatic: A trifle may cost tens of thousands; how can the treasury not run dry?

sentences.zh: 願屏絕淫巧，停罷宴遊，諸銀場及不急務悉為禁止。

translations.literal: We wish to shut out licentious ingenuity, stop and abolish banquets and excursions, and entirely forbid all silver mines and non-urgent undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to renounce extravagant novelties, suspend feasts and outings, and forbid silver mines and every nonessential project.

sentences.zh: 至兩京文武大臣，不乏奸貪，爭為蒙蔽。

translations.literal: As for civil and military great ministers of the two capitals, they are not lacking in treacherous greed, each striving to screen and conceal.
translations.idiomatic: Among civil and military ministers of both capitals, many are corrupt and compete to shield one another.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿謂其位高而不忍遽去，勿謂其舊臣而姑且寬容。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not say that because their rank is high you cannot bear to remove them quickly; must not say that because they are old ministers you will for the moment be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Do not spare them because their rank is high, nor indulge them because they are long-serving ministers.

sentences.zh: 宜令各自陳免，用全大體。

translations.literal: They should be ordered each to state his own request for dismissal, thereby to preserve the great body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Let each offer his resignation, that the integrity of government may be preserved.

sentences.zh: 其貪位不去者，則言官糾劾。

translations.literal: Those who greedily hold office and do not leave—then the remonstrance officials should impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who cling to office despite corruption should be impeached by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 而臣等濫居言路，無補於時，亦望罷歸，為不職戒。

translations.literal: As for your servants, who occupy the path of speech without warrant and bring no benefit to the age, we also hope to be dismissed and returned, as a warning against unworthy office.
translations.idiomatic: We who hold remonstrance posts without merit likewise beg dismissal, as a warning to the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒答之，然竟不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor with a gracious edict praised and answered them, yet in the end could not employ their advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict of praise, yet in the end adopted none of their recommendations.

sentences.zh: 元屢遷都給事中，出為福建右參政。

translations.literal: Yuan was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary-in-chief and was sent out as Right Administrative Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan rose repeatedly to supervising secretary-in-chief, then was appointed Right Administrative Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 巡視海道，嚴禁越海私販。

translations.literal: He inspected the sea routes and strictly forbade crossing the sea in private trade.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the coastal routes and strictly banned unauthorized overseas trade.

sentences.zh: 巨商以重寶賂，元怒叱出之。

translations.literal: Great merchants used heavy treasures to bribe him; Yuan angrily shouted and drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants tried to bribe him with costly gifts; Wei Yuan rebuked them furiously and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，廬墓三年，服除，起江西參政，卒。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he returned home, dwelt by the tomb three years; when mourning ended he was raised as Jiangxi Administrative Commissioner and died.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he retired to mourn at her tomb for three years; when the mourning period ended he was recalled as Administrative Commissioner of Jiangxi, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 康永韶，字用和，祁門人。

translations.literal: Kang Yongshao, style name Yonghe, was a man of Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yongshao, whose style was Yonghe, came from Qimen.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，入國學，選授御史。

translations.literal: He was raised in the provincial examination, entered the National University, and was selected and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination, entered the National University, and was selected as a censor.

sentences.zh: 成化初，巡按畿輔，劾尚書馬昂抑市民地。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, as touring inspector of the capital regions, he impeached Minister Ma Ang for suppressing commoners' land.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, while touring the capital districts, he impeached Minister Ma Ang for seizing commoners' land.

sentences.zh: 四年偕同官胡深、鄭己等爭慈懿太后山陵事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he joined colleagues in office Hu Shen, Zheng Ji, and others in disputing the mountain tomb affair of Empress Dowager Ciyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined colleagues Hu Shen, Zheng Ji, and others in the struggle over Empress Dowager Ciyi's burial.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，復偕同官上言八事，大旨與元前疏相類。

translations.literal: When the comet appeared, he again joined colleagues in office in submitting words on eight matters; the main purport resembled Yuan's former memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the comet appeared, he again joined his colleagues in a memorial on eight points, substantially echoing Wei Yuan's earlier submission.

sentences.zh: 兩京大臣考察庶寮，去留多不當。

translations.literal: Great ministers of the two capitals examined subordinate officials; who stayed and who left were mostly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When senior ministers of both capitals evaluated junior officials, many decisions of retention and dismissal were unjust.

sentences.zh: 永韶等復劾大臣行私，且摘刑部主事余誌等十二人罪，為誌所訐，俱下詔獄。

translations.literal: Yongshao and others again impeached the great ministers for private conduct, and moreover singled out twelve persons' crimes including Punishments Section director Yu Zhi; they were counter-impeached by Zhi, and all were sent to the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yongshao and his colleagues again impeached the ministers for favoritism and named twelve offenders, including director in the Ministry of Punishments Yu Zhi; Zhi struck back with accusations, and all were imprisoned by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 永韶謫順昌知縣，再調福清、惠安。

translations.literal: Yongshao was demoted to magistrate of Shunchang, then transferred again to Fuqing and Huian.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yongshao was demoted to magistrate of Shunchang, then reassigned to Fuqing and Huian in turn.

sentences.zh: 久之，有薦其知天文者，中旨召還，授欽天監正，進太常少卿，掌監事。

translations.literal: After a long while, someone recommended him for knowledge of astronomy; by middle edict he was summoned back, appointed Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, advanced to Vice Minister of Rites, and directed directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward someone recommended his knowledge of astronomy; an imperial rescript recalled him, appointed him Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, promoted him to Vice Minister of Rites, and put him in charge of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 永韶為御史有直聲，及是乃更迎合取寵，占候多隱諱，甚者以災為祥。

translations.literal: Yongshao as censor had a reputation for straight speech; reaching this point he then instead conformed and curried favor, and in prognostication mostly concealed and glossed over, in extreme cases treating disasters as auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: As a censor Kang Yongshao had enjoyed a reputation for blunt honesty; now he courted favor instead, concealing celestial warnings and even treating calamities as good omens.

sentences.zh: 陜西大饑，永韶言：「今春星變當有大咎，賴秦民饑死，足當之，誠國家無疆福。」

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered great famine; Yongshao said: "This spring stellar change ought to bring great calamity; relying on Qin people's starving to death, it is sufficient to answer it—truly the state's boundless fortune."
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi was stricken by famine, Kang Yongshao declared: "The stellar change this spring portends great disaster; thanks to the Qin people starving to death, the omen is fully answered—truly boundless fortune for the state."

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，中旨擢禮部右侍郎，仍掌監事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; by middle edict he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites, still directing directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and by rescript promoted him to Right Vice Minister of Rites while he retained charge of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 坐歷多訛字，落職歸。

translations.literal: Because the calendar had many erroneous characters, he was removed from office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the official calendar was found riddled with errors, he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 胡深，定遠衛人。

translations.literal: Hu Shen, a man of Dingyuan Guard.
