translations.idiomatic: Hu Shen came from Dingyuan Guard.

sentences.zh: 天順未進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate at the end of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the final years of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 既爭慈懿太后山陵事，復與同官陳宏、鄭己、何純、方昇、張進祿上疏請斥奸邪，痛詆學士商輅、尚書程信、姚夔、馬昂。

translations.literal: Having already disputed the mountain tomb affair of Empress Dowager Ciyi, he again joined colleagues in office Chen Hong, Zheng Ji, He Chun, Fang Sheng, and Zhang Jinlu in submitting a memorial asking to expel treacherous evil, bitterly denouncing Academician Shang Lu and Ministers Cheng Xin, Yao Kui, and Ma Ang.
translations.idiomatic: After the struggle over Empress Dowager Ciyi's burial, he joined colleagues Chen Hong, Zheng Ji, He Chun, Fang Sheng, and Zhang Jinlu in a memorial demanding the expulsion of corrupt ministers, savagely attacking Academician Shang Lu and Ministers Cheng Xin, Yao Kui, and Ma Ang.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 翌日給事中董旻、陳鶴、胡智亦劾輅等，疏呈御前。

translations.literal: The next day supervising secretaries Dong Min, Chen He, and Hu Zhi also impeached Lu and others, presenting the memorial before the sovereign in person.
translations.idiomatic: The next day supervising secretaries Dong Min, Chen He, and Hu Zhi also impeached Shang Lu and his colleagues, presenting the memorial directly before the throne.

sentences.zh: 故事，諫官彈章非大廷宣讀則封進，未有不讀而面呈者。

translations.literal: By precedent, remonstrance officials' impeachment documents, unless read aloud in the great court, were sealed and forwarded—never had there been one presented in person without being read.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, censors' impeachments were sealed and forwarded unless read in open court; never before had one been handed to the emperor in person without public reading.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，曰：「大臣進退有體，旻等敢不循舊章亂朝儀耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "Great ministers' advancement and withdrawal have proper form—do Min and the others dare not follow the old statutes and disorder court ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said, "Ministers rise and fall by established procedure—do Dong Min and his fellows dare disregard precedent and disrupt court ritual?"

sentences.zh: 輅等乞休，帝惟聽昂去。

translations.literal: Lu and others begged to retire; the emperor only permitted Ang to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu and the others begged to retire; the emperor allowed only Ma Ang to resign.

sentences.zh: 夔憤甚，連疏求去。

translations.literal: Kui was very angry and submitted memorials in succession asking to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Kui was furious and submitted memorial after memorial demanding dismissal.

sentences.zh: 深、旻等復合辭攻，而詆夔甚力。

translations.literal: Shen, Min, and others again joined words in attack, and denounced Kui with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shen, Dong Min, and the others renewed their assault in concert, heaping abuse on Yao Kui.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下深等九人獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent Shen and the other nine men to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger imprisoned Hu Shen and eight others.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史林誠亦嘗劾輅，不納，引病去，帝並屬誠吏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor Lin Cheng had also once impeached Lu; this was not accepted, and he cited illness and left—the emperor also handed Cheng over to the clerks of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Censor Lin Cheng had impeached Shang Lu without success and retired on grounds of illness; the emperor now handed Lin Cheng over to the judicial authorities as well.

sentences.zh: 毛弘等皆論救，輅亦請寬之，乃各杖二十，復其官。

translations.literal: Mao Hong and others all argued in rescue; Lu also asked that they be treated leniently—thereupon each was beaten twenty strokes and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hong and others pleaded for mercy; Shang Lu also asked leniency; each man received twenty strokes of the bastinado and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，深坐按陜時杖殺訴冤者，謫黔陽丞，稍遷郁林知州，卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Shen was convicted because while inspecting Shaanxi he beat to death one who pleaded injustice; he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Qianyang, then gradually promoted to prefect of Yulin, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hu Shen was found guilty of beating a petitioner to death while touring Shaanxi; he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Qianyang, later promoted to prefect of Yulin, and died there.

sentences.zh: 鄭己，山海衛人。

translations.literal: Zheng Ji, a man of Shanhai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ji came from Shanhai Guard.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 巡按陜西，請蠲邊地逋賦，分別邊兵，命壯者戰守，老弱耕牧，章下所司。

translations.literal: As touring inspector of Shaanxi, he requested remission of overdue taxes in border lands, distinguished border troops, and ordered the strong to fight and guard while the old and weak plowed and pastured—the memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Shaanxi he petitioned to remit overdue border taxes and reorganize frontier troops so the able-bodied fought and garrisoned while the old and weak farmed and herded; the memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 定西侯蔣琬鎮甘肅，己欲按其罪，語泄，為所劾，戍宣府。

translations.literal: Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan garrisoned Gansu; Ji wished to investigate his crimes, but the words leaked and he was impeached by Wan, and was garrisoned at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan commanded Gansu, Zheng Ji sought to prosecute him; word leaked out, Jiang Wan impeached him in turn, and he was banished to garrison duty at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 己性矜傲，時論不甚惜。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was proud and arrogant; opinion of the time did not greatly pity him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ji was proud and overbearing, and public opinion did not much lament his fall.

sentences.zh: 董旻，樂平人。

translations.literal: Dong Min, a man of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Min came from Leping.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 歷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of supervising secretary-in-chief of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising secretary-in-chief of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 為吏所訐，下詔獄，謫石臼知縣。

translations.literal: He was counter-impeached by clerks, sent to the edict prison, and demoted to magistrate of Shijiu.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks struck back with accusations; he was imprisoned by imperial order and demoted to magistrate of Shijiu.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時，卒官四川參議。

translations.literal: In the Xiaozong reign he died in office as Sichuan Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozong he died in office as Administrative Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 強珍，字廷貴，滄州人。

translations.literal: Qiang Zhen, style name Tinggui, was a man of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Zhen, whose style was Tinggui, came from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除涇縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jing County.

sentences.zh: 請減額賦，民德之。

translations.literal: He requested reduction of quota land tax; the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to reduce the assessed land tax, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 擢御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 初，遼東巡撫陳鉞啟釁召敵，敵至，務為蔽欺。

translations.literal: At first, the Liaodong grand coordinator Chen Yue provoked trouble and summoned the enemy; when the enemy arrived, he strove to conceal and deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, the Liaodong grand coordinator Chen Yue had provoked conflict and drawn the enemy in; when they came, he did everything he could to cover it up.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史王崇之劾鉞，鉞大恐。

translations.literal: The touring investigating censor Wang Chongzhi impeached Yue; Yue was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The touring investigating censor Wang Chongzhi impeached Chen Yue, and Chen was terrified.

sentences.zh: 謀之汪直，誣逮崇之下詔獄，輸贖，調延安推官。

translations.literal: He plotted with Wang Zhi, falsely charged and arrested Chongzhi, sending him to the imperial prison; after paying a redemption fee, he was transferred to be an administrator of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen colluded with the eunuch Wang Zhi to have Chongzhi seized on false charges and thrown into the imperial prison; after paying a redemption fine, Chongzhi was relegated to an administrator's post at Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 及直、鉞用兵，方論功而敵大入，中官韋朗、總兵官緱謙等匿不以聞。

translations.literal: When Zhi and Yue used troops, just as merit was being discussed the enemy poured in on a large scale; the eunuch Wei Lang, the regional commander Gou Qian, and others concealed it and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi and Chen Yue took the field, merit was still being debated when the enemy launched a major incursion; the eunuch Wei Lang, the regional commander Gou Qian, and others suppressed the news and never reported it.

sentences.zh: 珍往巡按，請正鉞罪。

translations.literal: Zhen went on a touring investigation and requested that Yue's crimes be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Zhen conducted a touring investigation and asked that Chen Yue be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書余子俊等奏鉞累犯重辟，不當貸。

translations.literal: The Minister of War Yu Zijun and others memorialized that Yue had repeatedly committed capital offenses and ought not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of War Yu Zijun and others submitted that Chen Yue had committed capital crimes repeatedly and should not be spared.

sentences.zh: 帝弗從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，指揮王全等誘殺朵顏衛人，珍發其狀，全等俱獲罪。

translations.literal: Before long, the commander Wang Quan and others lured and killed men of the Duoyan Guard; Zhen exposed the affair, and Quan and the rest were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Commander Wang Quan and others had treacherously killed men of the Duoyan Guard; Qiang Zhen exposed the crime, and Wang and his accomplices were all punished.

sentences.zh: 直方自矜有大功，聞珍疏怒。

translations.literal: Zhi had just been self-congratulatory about great merit; hearing Zhen's memorial, he grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was then congratulating himself on great achievements; when he heard of Qiang Zhen's memorial, he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 適巡邊還，鉞郊迎五十里，訴珍誣已，直益怒，奏珍所劾皆妄。

translations.literal: Just as he returned from touring the frontier, Yue went fifty li into the suburbs to welcome him and complained that Zhen had slandered him; Zhi grew angrier still and memorialized that all of Zhen's impeachments were false.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi had just returned from inspecting the frontier; Chen Yue went fifty li out to meet him and pleaded that Qiang Zhen had falsely accused him. Wang grew still angrier and submitted that every charge in Zhen's memorials was groundless.

sentences.zh: 詔遣錦衣千戶蕭聚往勘，械赴京。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Jinyi Guard thousand-household Xiao Ju to go investigate; Zhen was placed in the cangue and escorted to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Jinyi Guard officer Xiao Ju to go and investigate; Qiang Zhen was put in fetters and sent to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 比至，直先榜掠，然後奏聞，坐奏事不實，當輸贖。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Zhi first had him flogged on the rack, then reported to the throne; he was convicted of presenting false charges and sentenced to pay a redemption fee.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital, Wang Zhi had him beaten on the rack first and only then reported to the throne; he was found guilty of lodging false accusations and ordered to pay a redemption fine.

sentences.zh: 詔特謫戍遼東，而責兵部及言官先嘗劾鉞者。

translations.literal: An edict specially relegated him to garrison service in Liaodong and rebuked the Ministry of War and the remonstrating officials who had earlier impeached Yue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially banished him to garrison duty in Liaodong and blamed the Ministry of War and the remonstrance officials who had earlier impeached Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 居三年，直敗，復珍官，致仕。

translations.literal: After three years, Zhi fell from power; Zhen's office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, when Wang Zhi fell, Qiang Zhen was restored to office and then retired.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，起山東副使，擢大理少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, he was recalled as vice commissioner of Shandong and promoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongzhi reign he was recalled as administrative vice commissioner of Shandong and promoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 明年，以右僉都御史巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: The next year, he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 時緱謙已罷，珍奏留謙才力可用。

translations.literal: At that time Gou Qian had already been dismissed; Zhen memorialized to retain Qian, saying his talent and ability could still be used.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Qian had already been dismissed; Qiang Zhen memorialized that Qian's talents were still worth employing.

sentences.zh: 給事中言謙數失機，珍不應奏保，遂改南京右通政。

translations.literal: A supervising secretary said Qian had repeatedly missed opportunities; Zhen should not have memorialized to protect him, and he was thereupon transferred to right vice commissioner of communications at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: A supervising secretary objected that Gou Qian had repeatedly missed his chance; Qiang Zhen should never have recommended him, and Zhen was accordingly transferred to right vice commissioner of communications at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老乞休，久之卒。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of his mother's age, he requested leave to retire; after a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned to retire on grounds that his mother was elderly, and died some time later.

sentences.zh: 王瑞，字良璧，望江人。

translations.literal: Wang Rui, style name Liangbi, was a man of Wangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, whose style was Liangbi, came from Wangjiang.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.

sentences.zh: 嘗於文華殿抗言內寵滋甚，詞氣鯁直。

translations.literal: Once in the Wenhua Hall he spoke out against how inner favorites were growing more numerous; his words were blunt and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the Wenhua Hall he spoke out against the swelling ranks of palace favorites, his tone blunt and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，同列戰栗，瑞無懼色。

translations.literal: The emperor was thunderstruck with anger; his colleagues trembled, but Rui showed no sign of fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; his colleagues shook with fear, but Rui's face betrayed no alarm.

sentences.zh: 十五年疏請天下進表官各陳地方利病，帝惡其紛擾，杖之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he submitted a memorial asking that all officials coming to court with provincial memorials should each set forth local advantages and ills; the emperor hated the clutter and had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he memorialized that every official bearing provincial reports to court should speak to local strengths and abuses; the emperor disliked the uproar and had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 湖廣、江西撫、按官以所部災傷盜起，請免有司朝覲。

translations.literal: The grand coordinators and investigating censors of Huguang and Jiangxi, because their jurisdictions had suffered disasters and banditry had risen, asked that local officials be exempted from the annual court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinators and investigating censors of Huguang and Jiangxi, citing disasters and rising banditry in their jurisdictions, asked that local officials be excused from the annual court audience.

sentences.zh: 瑞等言：「歲侵民困，由有司不職，正當加罪，乃為請留。

translations.literal: Rui and others said: "Year after year of hardship has worn the people down; this is because officials are not performing their duties—they should be punished, yet you ask to keep them in place instead.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and others said: "Years of hardship have worn the people down because officials are derelict—they ought to be punished, yet you ask to keep them in post instead.

sentences.zh: 正官既留，則人才進退，何由審辨？

translations.literal: If the chief officials are kept, how can promotion and demotion of talent be judged?
translations.idiomatic: If chief officials are retained, how can the court judge who should rise and who should fall?

sentences.zh: 是朝覲、考察兩大典，皆從此廢壞矣。」

translations.literal: Thus the two great institutions of the court audience and triennial evaluation would both be ruined from this."
translations.idiomatic: In that way the two great institutions—the court audience and triennial evaluation—would both be wrecked."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，即命吏部禁之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their words and immediately ordered the Ministry of Personnel to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and at once ordered the Ministry of Personnel to forbid such exemptions.

sentences.zh: 進都給事中，言：「三載黜陟，朝廷大典。

translations.literal: Promoted to chief supervising secretary, he said: "The triennial promotion and demotion is a great institution of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to chief supervising secretary, he said: "The triennial review of appointments is one of the court's great institutions.

sentences.zh: 今布、按二司賢否，由撫、按牒報，其余由布、按評覆。

translations.literal: Now the worth of the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners is reported by the grand coordinators and investigating censors; the rest is reviewed by the provincial commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Today the merit of the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners is reported by grand coordinators and investigating censors, while everyone else is judged only through their review.

sentences.zh: 任情毀譽，多至失真。

translations.literal: Praise and blame at whim often reach the point of losing truth.
translations.idiomatic: Praise and blame given at whim often cease to reflect reality.

sentences.zh: 舉劾謬者，請連坐。」

translations.literal: Those whose recommendations and impeachments are wrong should, he requested, be punished by joint liability."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that officials who made mistaken recommendations or impeachments be punished by joint liability."

sentences.zh: 十九年冬，瑞以傳奉冗員淆亂仕路，率同官奏曰：「祖宗設官有定員，初無幸進之路，近始有納粟冠帶之制，然止榮其身，不任以職。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year, Rui, because supernumerary appointees were muddling the path of office, led his colleagues in memorializing: "The founding ancestors established offices with fixed quotas and at first had no path of favoritism; only recently did the system of buying grain for cap and belt appear, yet it only honored the person and did not assign duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the nineteenth year, Rui—because supernumerary appointees were corrupting the civil service—led his colleagues in a memorial: "Our founding ancestors fixed the number of offices and left no path of favoritism; only lately did the system of buying grain for cap and belt appear, and even then it honored the buyer alone without giving him duties.

sentences.zh: 今幸門大開，鬻販如市。

translations.literal: Now the gate of favor is wide open, and buying and selling are like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Now the gate of favor stands wide open, and offices are traded like goods in a market.

sentences.zh: 恩典內降，遍及吏胥。

translations.literal: Gracious favors issued from within reach even clerks and runners.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favors issued from within the palace reach even clerks and runners.

sentences.zh: 武階蔭襲，下逮白丁。

translations.literal: Military ranks by hereditary privilege extend down to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary military commissions descend even to men with no prior rank.

sentences.zh: 或選期未至，超越官資；

translations.literal: Some, before their selection term had arrived, leap over official seniority;
translations.idiomatic: Some advance beyond their seniority before their turn for selection has come;

sentences.zh: 或外任雜流，驟遷京職。

translations.literal: some in outside posts of miscellaneous rank are suddenly transferred to capital offices.
translations.idiomatic: others in minor provincial posts are suddenly moved into capital offices.

sentences.zh: 以至廝養賤夫、市井童稚，皆得攀援。

translations.literal: So that even menials, base fellows, market children, and youths all can climb by patronage.
translations.idiomatic: Until even stable boys, lowborn men, market children, and street youths can all climb by patronage.

sentences.zh: 妄竊名器，逾濫至此，有識寒心。

translations.literal: They presumptuously steal titles of honor; excess has reached this point—those with understanding are chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: They usurp titles of honor without warrant; excess has gone so far that thoughtful men are heartsick.

sentences.zh: 伏睹英廟復辟，景泰幸用者卒皆罷斥。

translations.literal: We have seen that when Emperor Ying returned to the throne, those whom Jingtai had favored by chance were in the end all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: We have seen that when Emperor Ying regained the throne, everyone Jingtai had favored by chance was eventually cast out.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦，天順冒功者一切革除。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty took the throne, all who had falsely claimed merit in the Tianshun era were entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, every Tianshun-era claimant of false merit was swept away.

sentences.zh: 乞斷自宸衷，悉皆斥汰，以存國體。」

translations.literal: We beg that Your Majesty decide from within the imperial breast and dismiss them all, to preserve the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Your Majesty decide from your own judgment and dismiss them all, to preserve the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 御史寶應張稷等亦言：「比來末流賤伎妄廁公卿，屠狗販繒濫居清要。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Zhang Ji of Baoying and others also said: "Recently base skills of the lowest sort presumptuously fill the ranks of dukes and ministers; butchers and silk peddlers occupy key posts in excess.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating censor Zhang Ji of Baoying and others also said: "Lately the lowest trades presumptuously fill the ranks of dukes and ministers; butchers and silk peddlers crowd the most sensitive offices.

sentences.zh: 文職有未識一丁，武階亦未挾一矢。

translations.literal: Among civil offices are some who cannot recognize a single character; among military ranks are some who have never carried a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Some civil officials cannot recognize a single character; some military officers have never drawn a bow.

sentences.zh: 白徒驟貴，間歲頻遷，或父子並坐一堂，或兄弟分踞各署。

translations.literal: Commoners are suddenly ennobled, promoted several times within a year; sometimes father and son sit in one hall together, or brothers divide themselves among separate offices.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners are suddenly ennobled and promoted several times within a year; sometimes father and son sit in one hall together, or brothers hold separate offices at once.

sentences.zh: 甚有軍匠逃匿，易姓進身；

translations.literal: There are even military artisans who flee and hide, change their surnames, and advance in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Some military artisans flee and hide, change their names, and win promotion;

sentences.zh: 官吏犯贓，隱罪希寵。

translations.literal: officials who committed corruption conceal their crimes and hope for favor.
translations.idiomatic: corrupt officials conceal their crimes and court favor instead.

sentences.zh: 一日而數十人得官，一署而數百人寄俸。

translations.literal: In a single day dozens of men receive offices; in a single bureau hundreds draw salaries in name only.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day dozens win office; in a single bureau hundreds draw salaries without serving.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，有如是之政令否也？」

translations.literal: Since antiquity, has there ever been government orders like these?"
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, has any dynasty issued orders like these?"

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，意頗動。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorials and his mind was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received these memorials, he was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 居三日，貶李孜省、淩中等四人秩，奪黃謙、錢通等九人官。

translations.literal: Within three days he reduced the rank of Li Zisheng, Ling Zhong, and four others, and stripped Huang Qian, Qian Tong, and nine others of office.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days he reduced the rank of Li Zisheng, Ling Zhong, and four others, and stripped Huang Qian, Qian Tong, and nine others of their offices.

sentences.zh: 人心快之。

translations.literal: People's hearts rejoiced at it.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，太監尚銘罷斥，而其黨李榮、蕭敬等猶用事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, the grand eunuch Shang Ming was dismissed, but his faction Li Rong, Xiao Jing, and others still held power.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the grand eunuch Shang Ming was dismissed, but his allies Li Rong, Xiao Jing, and others still held power.

sentences.zh: 瑞等復奏劾之，不從。

translations.literal: Rui and others again memorialized to impeach them; the emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and others memorialized again to impeach them, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 瑞居諫垣十余年，遷湖廣右參議，謝病歸，卒。

translations.literal: Rui dwelt in the remonstrance offices for more than ten years, was transferred to right administrative commissioner of Huguang, thanked the court for illness and returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rui served in the remonstrance offices for more than ten years, was transferred to right administrative commissioner of Huguang, retired on grounds of illness, and died.

sentences.zh: 李俊，字子英，岐山人。

translations.literal: Li Jun, style name Ziying, was a man of Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun, whose style was Ziying, came from Qishan.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除吏科給事中，屢遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section and was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section and was repeatedly promoted until he became chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十五年，帝以李孜省為太常寺丞，俊偕同官言：「孜省本贓吏，不宜玷清班，奉郊廟百神祀。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor made Li Zisheng vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jun together with his colleagues said: "Zisheng was originally a corrupt official and ought not stain the pure ranks or preside over the sacrifices to the hundred spirits at the suburban altars and temples."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor appointed Li Zisheng vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jun and his colleagues said: "Zisheng was originally a corrupt official. He ought not stain the pure ranks or preside over sacrifices to the hundred spirits at the suburban altars and temples."

sentences.zh: 會御史亦有言，乃改上林監副。

translations.literal: Investigating censors spoke as well; he was thereupon changed to vice director of the Imperial Park.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censors spoke as well, and Li was reassigned as vice director of the Imperial Park.

sentences.zh: 時汪直竊柄，陷馬文升、牟俸遣戍。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhi usurped power, entrapped Ma Wensheng and Mou Feng, and sent them to frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Zhi held power in secret and had Ma Wensheng and Mou Feng framed and banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝責言官不糾，杖俊及同官二十七人，御史王濬等二十九人。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed the remonstrance officials for not impeaching them and had Jun and twenty-seven colleagues beaten, and the investigating censor Wang Jun and twenty-nine others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed the remonstrance officials for failing to impeach Wang and had Jun and twenty-seven colleagues beaten, along with investigating censor Wang Jun and twenty-nine others.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝耽於燕樂，群小亂政，屢致災譴。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was addicted to feasting and music; petty men threw government into disorder and repeatedly brought down heavenly warnings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was lost in feasting and music; petty men threw government into disorder, and heaven sent warning after warning.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年正月朔申刻，有星西流，化白氣，聲如雷。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year, at the third quarter of the first day of the first month, a star flowed westward, turned into white vapor, and sounded like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, at the third quarter of the first day of the first month, a star streaked westward, dissolved into white vapor, and thundered like an explosion.

sentences.zh: 帝頗懼，詔求直言，俊率六科諸臣上疏曰：

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat afraid and issued an edict seeking blunt speech; Jun led the officials of the six sections in submitting a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken and issued an edict calling for blunt counsel; Jun led the officials of the six sections in a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 今之弊政最大且急者，曰近幸幹紀也，大臣不職也，爵賞太濫也，工役過煩也，進獻無厭也，流亡未復也。

translations.literal: Of present abuses in government, the greatest and most urgent are these: favorites near the throne violating discipline; great ministers not performing their duties; titles and rewards too lavish; labor service too burdensome; tribute offerings without end; and exiles not yet restored.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest and most urgent abuses in government today are these: palace favorites who violate discipline; great ministers who neglect their duties; titles and rewards dispensed too freely; labor service imposed too heavily; tribute offered without end; and refugees not yet restored to their homes.

sentences.zh: 天變之來，率由於此。

translations.literal: Heavenly changes come, as a rule, from these causes.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly warnings come, as a rule, from these causes.

sentences.zh: 夫內侍之設，國初皆有定制。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of inner attendants, at the founding of the state there were fixed regulations for all.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants were established at the founding of the dynasty under fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 今或一監而叢一二十人，或一事而參五六七輩；

translations.literal: Now sometimes one bureau has a cluster of ten or twenty men, or one affair involves five, six, or seven groups;
translations.idiomatic: Today one bureau may hold a cluster of ten or twenty men, or one task may involve five, six, or seven groups;

sentences.zh: 或分布藩郡，享王者之奉；

translations.literal: some are distributed through feudatory commanderies and enjoy a king's stipend;
translations.idiomatic: some are posted through the provinces and enjoy stipends fit for a king;

sentences.zh: 或總領邊疆，專大將之權；

translations.literal: some command the frontier in chief and monopolize a great general's authority;
translations.idiomatic: some command the frontier and monopolize a great general's authority;

sentences.zh: 或依憑左右，援引憸邪；

translations.literal: some rely on the emperor's side and draw in the crafty and wicked;
translations.idiomatic: some cling to the emperor's side and draw in the crafty and wicked;

sentences.zh: 或交通中外，投獻奇巧。

translations.literal: some traffic between inside and outside and present strange contrivances.
translations.idiomatic: some traffic between court and country and present strange contrivances as gifts.

sentences.zh: 司錢谷則法外取財，貢方物則多端責賂，兵民坐困，官吏蒙殃。

translations.literal: Those who manage money and grain take wealth outside the law; those who present local products exact bribes in many ways—soldiers and people sit in distress, officials suffer calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Those who manage revenue extort wealth beyond the law; those who present local products demand bribes by every means—soldiers and civilians suffer, and officials are ruined.

sentences.zh: 殺人者見原，僨事者逃罪。

translations.literal: Killers are pardoned; those who stir up trouble escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers are pardoned; troublemakers escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 如梁芳、韋興、陳喜輩，不可枚舉。

translations.literal: Such men as Liang Fang, Wei Xing, and Chen Xi cannot be counted one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Liang Fang, Wei Xing, and Chen Xi are too many to list.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下大施剛斷，無令幹紀，奉使於外者悉為召還，用事於內者嚴加省汰；

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty greatly exercises firm resolve, does not let them violate discipline, recalls all who serve on missions outside, and strictly reduces those who hold power within;
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty acts with firm resolve—stopping their violations of discipline, recalling every eunuch sent on outside missions, and strictly cutting back those who hold power within—

sentences.zh: 則近幸戢而天意可回矣。

translations.literal: then favorites near the throne will be restrained and heaven's intent can be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: will palace favorites be restrained and heaven's intent turned back.

sentences.zh: 今之大臣，其未進也，非夤緣內臣則不得進；

translations.literal: Among present great ministers, before they advance, if they do not curry favor with inner attendants they cannot advance;
translations.idiomatic: Among today's great ministers, before they rise, none can advance without currying favor with inner attendants;

sentences.zh: 其既進也，非依憑內臣則不得安。

translations.literal: after they have advanced, if they do not rely on inner attendants they cannot be secure.
translations.idiomatic: and after they rise, none can keep his place without relying on inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 此以財貿官，彼以官鬻財，無怪其漁獵四方，而轉輸權貴也。

translations.literal: These trade wealth for office, those sell office for wealth—no wonder they plunder in all directions and convey goods to the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: They trade wealth for office and office for wealth—no wonder they plunder the realm and ship their gains to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 如尚書殷謙、張鵬、李本，侍郎艾福、杜銘、劉俊，皆既老且懦。

translations.literal: Such as the ministers Yin Qian, Zhang Peng, and Li Ben, and the vice ministers Ai Fu, Du Ming, and Liu Jun, are all already old and timid.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers such as Yin Qian, Zhang Peng, and Li Ben, and vice ministers such as Ai Fu, Du Ming, and Liu Jun, are all old and timid.

sentences.zh: 尚書張鎣、張瑄，侍郎尹直，大理卿田景旸，皆清論不愜。

translations.literal: The ministers Zhang Ying and Zhang Xuan, the vice minister Yin Zhi, and the president of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Jingyang all have pure discourse that does not please.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Zhang Ying and Zhang Xuan, vice minister Yin Zhi, and Court of Judicial Review president Tian Jingyang all speak uprightly but displease those in power.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下大加黜罰，勿為姑息，則大臣知警而天意可回矣。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty greatly increases dismissals and punishments and does not show indulgence will great ministers know to take warning and heaven's intent can be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty dismisses and punishes them severely, without indulgence, will great ministers take warning and heaven's intent be turned back.

sentences.zh: 夫爵以待有德，賞以待有功也。

translations.literal: Titles are to await the worthy; rewards are to await the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: Titles exist to honor the worthy; rewards exist to honor merit.

sentences.zh: 今或無故而爵一庸流，或無功而賞一貴幸。

translations.literal: Now sometimes without cause a title is given to a worthless fellow, or without merit a favorite is rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Today titles are sometimes given without cause to worthless men, and rewards without merit to court favorites.

sentences.zh: 祈雨雪者得美官，進金寶者射厚利。

translations.literal: Those who pray for rain and snow receive fine offices; those who present gold and jewels aim at thick profits.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pray for rain win fine offices; those who present gold and jewels reap heavy profits.

sentences.zh: 方士獻煉服之書，伶人奏曼延之戲。

translations.literal: Daoist masters present books on refining elixirs for ingestion; actors perform sprawling entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist masters present books on elixirs of immortality; actors perform sprawling entertainments.

sentences.zh: 掾史胥徒皆叨官祿，俳優僧道亦玷班資。

translations.literal: Clerks, runners, and attendants all receive official salaries in vain; actors, monks, and Daoists also stain the ranks and stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks, runners, and attendants all draw official salaries without warrant; actors, monks, and Daoists also stain the civil ranks.

sentences.zh: 一歲而傳奉或至千人，數歲而數千人矣。

translations.literal: In one year supernumerary appointees may reach a thousand; in several years there are several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In a single year supernumerary appointees may reach a thousand; within a few years there are several thousand.

sentences.zh: 數千人之祿，歲以數十萬計。

translations.literal: The salaries of several thousand men amount to hundreds of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: Their salaries amount to hundreds of thousands of taels each year.

sentences.zh: 是皆國之命脈，民之脂膏，可以養賢士，可以活饑民，誠可惜也。

translations.literal: These are all the lifeblood of the state and the fat and cream of the people; they could nourish worthy scholars and could keep starving people alive—truly it is a pity.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is the lifeblood of the state and the fat of the people—wealth that could nourish worthy scholars and keep starving people alive. It is a grievous waste.

sentences.zh: 方士道流如左通政李孜省、太常少卿鄧常恩輩，尤為誕妄，此招天變之甚者。

translations.literal: Daoist masters and religious adepts such as the left vice commissioner of communications Li Zisheng and the vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Deng Chang'en are especially absurd and delusive; this is what most gravely summons heavenly change.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist masters such as left vice commissioner of communications Li Zisheng and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Deng Chang'en are especially absurd; they above all summon heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 乞盡罷傳奉之官，毋令汙玷朝列，則爵賞不濫而天意可回矣。

translations.literal: We beg that all supernumerary offices be entirely abolished and not allowed to stain and defile the court ranks; then titles and rewards will not be excessive and heaven's intent can be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that all supernumerary offices be abolished and kept from staining the court ranks; then titles and rewards will no longer be lavished without warrant and heaven's intent will be turned back.

sentences.zh: 今都城佛剎迄無寧工，京營軍士不復遺力。

translations.literal: Now Buddhist monasteries in the capital have never had a peaceful end to work; soldiers of the capital garrison no longer spare their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist monasteries in the capital never see work cease; soldiers of the capital garrison are driven without rest.

sentences.zh: 如國師繼曉假術濟私，糜耗特甚，中外切齒。

translations.literal: Such as the state preceptor Ji Xiao, who borrowed techniques to serve private ends, wasted and consumed to an extreme degree—inside and outside gnash their teeth at it.
translations.idiomatic: The state preceptor Ji Xiao, for example, used religious pretenses for private gain and wasted resources on a shocking scale; men inside and outside the court gnash their teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 願陛下內惜資財，外惜人力，不急之役姑賜停罷，則工役不煩而天意可回矣。

translations.literal: We wish that Your Majesty within cherish resources and wealth and without cherish human strength; non-urgent labor services be for now granted cessation—then labor service will not be burdensome and heaven's intent can be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Your Majesty cherish the treasury within and labor without, and for now suspend every non-urgent project; then forced labor will no longer burden the realm and heaven's intent will be turned back.

sentences.zh: 近來規利之徒，率假進奉以耗國財。

translations.literal: Recently profit-seeking persons for the most part falsely use tribute presentations to drain state wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Of late, men who scheme for profit routinely cloak their greed in false tribute presentations, draining the national treasury.

sentences.zh: 或錄一方書，市一玩器，購一畫圖，制一簪珥，所費不多，獲利十倍。

translations.literal: Some copy one prescription book, buy one curio, purchase one painting, make one hairpin or earring—the expenditure is not much, profit tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: A copied medical text, a trinket, a painting, a hairpin or earring—little is spent, yet the profit may be tenfold.

sentences.zh: 願陛下洞燭此弊，留府庫之財為軍國之備，則進獻息而天意可回矣。

translations.literal: We wish that Your Majesty see through this evil clearly, keep treasury wealth for military and state preparations—then tribute presentations will cease and heaven's intent can be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Your Majesty see through this abuse, keep treasury funds for military and state needs, and let such presentations cease; then heaven's intent will be turned back.

sentences.zh: 陜西、河南、山西赤地千里。

translations.literal: Shaanxi, Henan, and Shanxi—bare earth for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi, Henan, and Shanxi the land lies barren for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 屍骸枕籍，流亡日多，萑苻可慮。

translations.literal: Corpses piled pillow to mat, exiles daily increase, thicket-bandits are to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses lie heaped upon one another, exiles grow daily, and outlaw bands are a growing menace.

sentences.zh: 願體天心之仁愛，憫生民之困窮，追錄貴幸鹽課，暫假造寺資財，移振饑民，俾茍存活，則流亡復而天意可回矣。

translations.literal: We wish to embody heaven's heart of benevolence, pity the people's hardship and poverty, recover salt revenues of the honored and favored, temporarily borrow temple-building funds, shift to relieve famine victims and enable them barely to survive—then exiles will return and heaven's intent can be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Your Majesty embody heaven's compassion, pity the people's distress, recover salt revenues granted the privileged, temporarily divert funds for temple building to famine relief, and keep the starving barely alive; then the exiles will return and heaven's intent will be turned back.

sentences.zh: 夫天下譬之人身。

translations.literal: Now the realm is like the human body.
translations.idiomatic: The realm may be compared to the human body.

sentences.zh: 人主，元首也；

translations.literal: The sovereign is the head;
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is the head;

sentences.zh: 大臣，股肱也；

translations.literal: great ministers are the arms and legs;
translations.idiomatic: great ministers are the arms and legs;

sentences.zh: 諫官，耳目也；

translations.literal: remonstrating officials are the eyes and ears;
translations.idiomatic: remonstrating officials are the eyes and ears;

sentences.zh: 京師，腹心也；

translations.literal: the capital is the belly and heart;
translations.idiomatic: the capital is the belly and heart;

sentences.zh: 藩郡，軀幹也。

translations.literal: provincial commanderies are the trunk.
translations.idiomatic: the provinces are the trunk.

sentences.zh: 大臣不職則股肱痿痹，諫官緘默則耳目塗塞，京師不職則腹心受病，藩郡災荒則軀幹削弱，元首豈能宴然而安哉？

translations.literal: If great ministers do not perform their duties then arms and legs wither and become numb; if remonstrating officials keep silent then eyes and ears are smeared and blocked; if the capital does not perform its duties then belly and heart suffer illness; if provincial commanderies suffer disaster and famine then the trunk is weakened—how can the head rest at ease in feasting?
translations.idiomatic: When ministers neglect their duties the limbs grow numb; when remonstrators fall silent the senses are stopped; when the capital fails the heart is stricken; when the provinces suffer famine the trunk is enfeebled—how then can the head rest at ease?

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下聽言必行，事天以實。

translations.literal: We prostrate ourselves hoping Your Majesty will hear words and surely act, serve heaven with substance.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Your Majesty heed counsel and act upon it, and serve heaven in deed, not show.

sentences.zh: 疏斥群小，親近賢臣。

translations.literal: Keep distant and expel the petty crowd, draw near worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Keep petty men at a distance and draw worthy ministers close.

sentences.zh: 咨治道之得失，究前代之興亡。

translations.literal: Consult on the gains and losses of the way of governance, investigate the rise and fall of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Inquire into what has succeeded and failed in governance, and study how former dynasties rose and fell.

sentences.zh: 以聖賢之經代方書，以文學之臣代方士。

translations.literal: Use the classics of sages and worthies in place of prescription books, use literary officials in place of recipe masters.
translations.idiomatic: Let the classics of sages replace occult manuals, and men of letters replace recipe masters.

sentences.zh: 則必有正誼足以廣聖學，讜論足以究天變。

translations.literal: Then there will surely be upright righteousness sufficient to broaden sagely learning, and forthright discourse sufficient to investigate heavenly changes.
translations.idiomatic: Then upright doctrine will broaden the sage's teaching, and honest counsel will probe heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 而手足便利，耳目聰明，腹心安泰，軀幹強健，元首於是乎大明矣。

translations.literal: Then hands and feet will be convenient, eyes and ears clear and keen, belly and heart peaceful and secure, trunk strong and robust—the head thereby will be greatly illumined.
translations.idiomatic: Then the limbs will be nimble, the senses keen, the heart at peace, the trunk strong, and the head will shine forth in full clarity.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor with gracious edict replied to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 降孜省上林丞，常恩本寺丞，繼曉革國師為民，令巡按御史追其誥敕。

translations.literal: Demoted Zisheng to director of the imperial parks, Chang'en to his original temple director, Ji Xiao stripped of state preceptor and made a commoner, ordered touring censors to recover their patents of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zisheng was demoted to director of the imperial parks, Deng Chang'en to his former temple post, Ji Xiao stripped of the title state preceptor and reduced to commoner status, and touring censors were ordered to recover their patents of appointment.

sentences.zh: 制下，舉朝大悅。

translations.literal: When the decree was issued, the whole court was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the decree was issued, the whole court rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 五月，俊出為湖廣布政司參議。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Jun was sent out as Hunan Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Li Jun was posted out as vice commissioner of the Hunan provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，屢官山西參政，卒。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi era he repeatedly served as Shanxi Vice Commissioner and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi he rose repeatedly to vice commissioner in Shanxi, and there died.

sentences.zh: 汪奎，字文燦，婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Kui, courtesy name Wencan, a man of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui, courtesy name Wencan, was a native of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 為秀水知縣，擢御史。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Xiushui and was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Xiushui, then was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，星變，偕同官疏陳十事，言：

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the stars changed, together with colleagues he memorialized setting forth ten matters, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Chenghua, when a celestial anomaly occurred, he joined his colleagues in a memorial setting forth ten matters, which read:

sentences.zh: 「建言貶謫諸臣，效忠於國，宜復其職。

translations.literal: The various officials who offered counsel and were demoted and banished have been loyal to the state—they should be restored to their offices.
translations.idiomatic: "Officials who spoke up and were demoted have served the state faithfully; they should be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 妖僧繼曉結中官梁芳，耗竭內藏，乞治芳罪，斬繼曉都市。

translations.literal: The demonic monk Ji Xiao joined with eunuch Liang Fang and drained the inner treasury—we beg that Fang be punished and Ji Xiao be beheaded in the market of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-monk Ji Xiao colluded with the eunuch Liang Fang and drained the inner treasury; we ask that Fang be punished and Ji Xiao beheaded in the capital marketplace.

sentences.zh: 傳奉官顧賢等皆中官恒從子而冒錦衣，李孜省小吏而授通政，宜盡斥以清仕路。

translations.literal: Supernumerary officials such as Gu Xian are all constant followers of eunuchs who usurped brocade-robe guard rank; Li Zisheng was a petty clerk yet granted vice commissioner of communications—all should be entirely expelled to clear the path of office.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary appointees such as Gu Xian are eunuchs' hangers-on who wear brocade-guard rank without warrant; Li Zisheng was a petty clerk yet made vice commissioner of communications—all should be dismissed to clear the path of office.

sentences.zh: 尚書殷謙、李本，侍郎杜銘、尹直，皆素乏清譽，尚書張鵬、張鎣、張瑄，侍郎杜謙、艾福、馬顯、劉俊，大理卿宋欽，巡撫都御史魯能、馬馴，皆老懦無能，侍郎談倫奔競無恥，巡撫趙文博粗鄙妄為，大理卿田景旸素行不謹，宜令致仕。

translations.literal: Ministers Yin Qian and Li Ben, vice ministers Du Ming and Yin Zhi—all have long lacked clean reputation; ministers Zhang Peng, Zhang Ying, and Zhang Xuan, vice ministers Du Qian, Ai Fu, Ma Xian, and Liu Jun, chief grand coordinator of the Court of Judicial Review Song Qin, grand coordinators Lu Neng and Ma Xun—all are old, timid, and incapable; vice minister Tan Lun is scrambling and shameless; grand coordinator Zhao Wenbo is crude, vulgar, and reckless; chief grand coordinator Tian Jingyang's conduct has long been unseemly—they should all be ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Yin Qian and Li Ben and vice ministers Du Ming and Yin Zhi have long lacked clean reputations; ministers Zhang Peng, Zhang Ying, and Zhang Xuan, vice ministers Du Qian, Ai Fu, Ma Xian, and Liu Jun, chief grand coordinator Song Qin, and grand coordinators Lu Neng and Ma Xun are old, timid, and incapable; vice minister Tan Lun is shamelessly ambitious; grand coordinator Zhao Wenbo is crude and reckless; chief grand coordinator Tian Jingyang's conduct has long been unseemly—all should be ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 鎮守、守備內官視天順間逾數倍，作威福，淩虐有司。

translations.literal: Inner eunuchs as garrison commanders and defense commanders exceed several times those of the Tianshun era, wielding authority and blessings, bullying and abusing regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch garrison and defense commanders now outnumber those of the Tianshun reign several times over; they wield arbitrary power and bully civil officials.

sentences.zh: 浙江張慶、四川蔡用得逮治四品以下官，尤傷國體，宜悉撤還。

translations.literal: Zhang Qing of Zhejiang and Cai Yongde of Sichuan have arrested and tried officials of the fourth rank and below—this especially wounds the state's dignity; they should all be withdrawn and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qing in Zhejiang and Cai Yongde in Sichuan have arrested and tried officials of the fourth rank and below, gravely wounding the dignity of the state; they should all be recalled.

sentences.zh: 內外坐營、監槍內官增置過多，皆私役軍士，辦納月錢，多者至二三百人。

translations.literal: Inner and outer camp-sitting and firearm-supervising eunuchs have been added in excessive numbers; all privately impress soldiers and collect monthly payments—some have as many as two or three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs attached to camps inside and outside the capital have been multiplied far beyond need; all privately impress soldiers and exact monthly payments from them, some keeping as many as two or three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 武將亦皆私役健丁，行伍惟存老弱。

translations.literal: Military officers also all privately impress sturdy youths; in the ranks only the old and weak remain.
translations.idiomatic: Generals too privately impress sturdy youths for their households, leaving only the old and weak in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 勛戚、內官奏乞鹽利，滿載南行，所至張欽賜黃旗，商旅不行，邊儲虧損，並宜嚴禁。

translations.literal: Meritorious kin and inner eunuchs memorialize begging salt profits, load full boats and travel south; wherever they go they display imperial-bestowed yellow banners, merchants and travelers cannot pass, border stores suffer loss—all should be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious kin and palace eunuchs petition for salt monopolies and travel south with laden boats, displaying imperial yellow banners wherever they go so that merchants cannot pass and border stores are depleted—all of this should be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 陜西、山西、河南頻年水旱，死徙大半，山、陜之民僅存無幾。

translations.literal: Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan for successive years have flood and drought; dead and displaced are more than half; the people of the mountains and Shaanxi barely survive, few remaining.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Henan have suffered flood and drought year after year; more than half the people are dead or displaced, and scarcely any remain in the mountain districts and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 宜核被災郡縣，概與蠲除。

translations.literal: It is fitting to verify disaster-struck commanderies and counties and broadly grant remission and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: The stricken commanderies and counties should be surveyed and taxes broadly remitted.

sentences.zh: 給事張善吉先坐罪謫官，考績至京，昏夜乞憐，得授茲職，大玷清班，宜罷斥。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhang Shanji first was convicted and demoted to official; when his performance review brought him to the capital, in dark night he begged for pity and obtained this post—greatly staining the pure ranks; he should be dismissed and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhang Shanji was first convicted and demoted; when he came to the capital for his performance review he begged for mercy by night and won this post, gravely staining the pure ranks—he should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 山、陜、河、洛饑民多流鄖、襄，至骨肉相啖。

translations.literal: Famine victims of the mountains, Shaanxi, the Yellow River region, and Luoyang mostly drifted to Yun and Xiang, reaching the point that flesh and bone ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Starving people from the mountain districts, Shaanxi, the Yellow River basin, and Luoyang streamed into Yun and Xiang, until kin ate kin.

sentences.zh: 請大發帑庾振濟，消弭他變。」

translations.literal: We request greatly issuing treasury granaries for relief and assistance, to dispel and extinguish other changes."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that the treasury be opened wide for famine relief, lest other calamities follow."

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝以災變求言，奎疏入，雖觸帝忌，未加譴。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor because of disaster and change sought counsel; when Kui's memorial entered, although it touched the emperor's taboos, he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor, moved by celestial warnings, had called for candid counsel; when Kui's memorial arrived, though it touched the emperor's sore points, he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 無何，有御史失儀，奎當面糾，退朝乃奏。

translations.literal: Before long, a censor lost decorum; Kui corrected him to his face, and only after leaving court did he memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a censor breached court decorum; Kui rebuked him to his face but filed his memorial only after court had adjourned.

sentences.zh: 帝以其怠緩，杖之於廷。

translations.literal: The emperor because of his slackness and delay had him beaten in the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him dilatory and had him beaten in court.

sentences.zh: 居數月，復出為夔州通判，討平雲陽劇賊。

translations.literal: After several months he was again sent out as Tongzhou subprefect of Kuizhou and suppressed fierce bandits of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was again posted out as subprefect of Kuizhou and put down fierce bandits in Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，量移敘州同知。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended, he was transferred by degree to Tongzhi of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne, Kui was transferred laterally to assistant prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以薦，擢成都知府。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted to prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was promoted to prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 歲饑多盜，振救多復業。

translations.literal: In years of famine there were many bandits; relief and rescue brought many back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years banditry was rife, but relief work brought many back to their trades.

sentences.zh: 三遷廣西左布政使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Left Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became left administration commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年以右副都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he grand-coordinated Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi (1501) he was appointed grand coordinator of Guizhou with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未浹歲，普安賊婦米魯作亂，被劾致仕。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, the bandit woman Milu of Pu'an raised rebellion; he was impeached and ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed the bandit woman Milu of Pu'an rose in rebellion; impeached, he was forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 正德六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Zhengde (1511).

sentences.zh: 從子舜民，字從仁。

translations.literal: His nephew Shunmin, courtesy name Congren.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wang Shunmin, courtesy name Congren.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢御史，出按甘肅。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier, promoted to censor, and sent out to investigate Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier, then promoted to censor and sent to investigate Gansu.

sentences.zh: 劾中官將帥失事，陳邊計，章數十上。

translations.literal: He impeached eunuchs and generals for failures, set forth border plans, and memorialized dozens of times.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached eunuchs and generals for their failures, set forth border strategy, and submitted dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 先是，奎杖闕下，舜民扶掖之，帝聞而怒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kui was beaten beneath the gate-tower, Shunmin supported and assisted him; the emperor heard and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Kui was beaten beneath the palace gate, Shunmin had supported him; the emperor heard of it and was enraged.

sentences.zh: 至是，奏獄情詞不當，貶蒙化衛經歷。

translations.literal: At this time, because his memorial on prison facts used improper wording, he was demoted to administrative aide of the Mengzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because a memorial on a prison case used improper wording, he was demoted to administrative aide of the Menghua Guard.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，遷知東莞，未上，擢江西僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was transferred to magistrate of Dongguan; before taking up the post he was promoted to Jiangxi Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was appointed magistrate of Dongguan, but before he took up the post he was promoted to vice commissioner in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 善讞獄，剖析如流。

translations.literal: He was skilled at deciding cases, dissecting and analyzing like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at judging cases, unraveling them with fluent clarity.

sentences.zh: 其清軍法，後人遵守之。

translations.literal: His method for clearing the military rolls, later men observed and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: His regulations for clearing the military rolls were observed by later generations.

sentences.zh: 改雲南屯田副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Yunnan Vice Commissioner for Garrison Fields.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner for garrison fields in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 田為勢要奪者，厘而歸之官。

translations.literal: Fields seized by powerful persons he rectified and returned to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Land seized by the powerful he surveyed and restored to official control.

sentences.zh: 麓川遺孽思祿渡金沙江，據孟密，承檄撫定之。

translations.literal: The remnant scion of Lucuan, Silu, crossed the Jinsha River and seized Mengmi; on receiving the dispatch he pacified and settled it.
translations.idiomatic: Silu, a remnant of the Lucuan line, crossed the Jinsha River and seized Mengmi; on receipt of his commission he pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服除，適淮、揚大饑，以故官奉命振濟。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, just as Huai and Yang suffered great famine, in his former office he received orders to relieve and assist.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, a great famine struck the Huai and Yang regions, and in his former capacity he was ordered to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 用便宜發粟，奏停不急務，活饑民百二十萬人，流冗復業者八千余戶。

translations.literal: Using discretionary authority he issued grain, memorialized to halt non-urgent tasks, kept alive 1.2 million famine victims, and among drifting redundant persons more than eight thousand households returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Exercising discretionary authority he released grain, memorialized to suspend non-urgent projects, kept 1.2 million famine victims alive, and saw more than eight thousand displaced households return to their trades.

sentences.zh: 進福建按察使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Fujian Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 盜竊福清縣庫，或誣其怨家，已成獄。

translations.literal: Thieves stole the Fuqing county treasury; some falsely accused their enemies, and the case had already become a closed verdict.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fuqing county treasury was robbed, some accused their personal enemies, and the case had already been closed.

sentences.zh: 舜民廉得真盜，脫三十人於死，抵誣者罪。

translations.literal: Shunmin through investigation obtained the true thieves, freed thirty men from death, and imposed punishment on the false accusers.
translations.idiomatic: Shunmin's investigation uncovered the real thieves, spared thirty men from execution, and punished the false accusers.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，禱不應。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, prayers did not receive response.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year his prayers for rain went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 躬蒞福州獄，釋枉系輕罪者，所部有司皆清獄，遂大雨。

translations.literal: He personally went to Fuzhou prisons, released those wrongly detained for light offenses, and all officials in his jurisdiction cleared their prisons—then great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person to the Fuzhou prisons, released those wrongly held on light charges, and ordered every subordinate jurisdiction to clear its jails; then heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 歷河南左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He passed through Left and Right Administration Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 正德二年以右副都御史撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he governed and pacified Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde (1507) he was appointed to govern Yunyang with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，罷天下巡撫官，改蒞南京都察院，道卒。

translations.literal: Barely one month later, all grand coordinators under heaven were abolished; he was changed to take charge of the Nanjing Censorate and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later grand coordinators were abolished empire-wide; he was reassigned to the Nanjing Censorate and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 奎性簡靜，不茍取與，以篤實見稱。

translations.literal: Kui's nature was simple and quiet; he was not careless in giving and taking, and was praised for solid sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was plain and reserved, scrupulous in his dealings, and praised for steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 而舜民好學砥行，矯矯持風節，尤負時望。

translations.literal: Shunmin loved learning and polished conduct, loftily upheld moral integrity, and especially bore the hopes of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Shunmin loved learning and cultivated his conduct, holding his principles with conspicuous firmness, and enjoyed exceptional esteem among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 方星變求言時，九卿各條奏數事，率有所避，無甚激切者，唯奎與李俊等言最直。

translations.literal: When the stars changed and counsel was sought, the nine ministers each memorialized in items several matters—for the most part they had something they avoided, none very sharp and urgent; only Kui and Li Jun and others spoke most directly.
translations.idiomatic: When the celestial anomaly prompted the call for counsel, the nine ministers each submitted several items, but mostly hedged their words and none spoke with great force; only Kui and Li Jun and a few others were most blunt.

sentences.zh: 而武選員外郎崔升、彭綱，主事蘇章，戶部主事周軫，刑部主事李旦皆有言。

translations.literal: Moreover, Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments Cui Sheng and Peng Gang, Section Chief Su Zhang, Section Chief of the Ministry of Revenue Zhou Zhen, and Section Chief of the Ministry of Justice Li Dan all had words to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Bureau of Military Appointments Cui Sheng and Peng Gang, section chief Su Zhang, section chief of revenue Zhou Zhen, and section chief of justice Li Dan also spoke up.

sentences.zh: 升、章言宦官妖僧罪，請亟誅竄，而尚書王恕今伊、傅，不宜置南京。

translations.literal: Sheng and Zhang spoke on the crimes of eunuchs and demonic monks, begging urgent execution and banishment; moreover Minister Wang Su is now Yi and Fu—it is not fitting to place him in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Zhang denounced the crimes of eunuchs and sorcerer-monks and begged swift execution and banishment; they also argued that Minister Wang Su, a man fit to be Yi Yin or Fu Yue to the throne, should not be left in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 綱斥李孜省、繼曉，請誅之以謝天下。

translations.literal: Gang denounced Li Zisheng and Ji Xiao, begging their execution to appease all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Gang denounced Li Zisheng and Ji Xiao and asked that they be executed to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 軫亦請誅梁芳、李孜省，並汰內侍，罷方書。

translations.literal: Zhen also begged execution of Liang Fang and Li Zisheng, and together pruning inner attendants and abolishing prescription books.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen likewise demanded the execution of Liang Fang and Li Zisheng, a reduction of palace attendants, and an end to occult manuals.

sentences.zh: 旦陳十事，且言：「神仙、佛老、外戚、女謁，聲色貨利，奇技淫巧，皆陛下素所惑溺，而左右近習交相誘之。」

translations.literal: Dan set forth ten matters, and moreover said: "Immortals, Buddhist and Daoist adepts, maternal kin, female petitioners, sound and color, goods and profit, strange skills and excessive craft—all are what Your Majesty has long been deluded and drowned in, while those near at hand on left and right mutually entice you."
translations.idiomatic: Dan set forth ten matters, adding: "Immortals, Buddhist and Daoist adepts, consort kin, female petitioners, music and women, wealth and gain, strange arts and lavish crafts—these are what Your Majesty has long been steeped in, while those close at hand egg one another on to lead you deeper."

sentences.zh: 言甚切。

translations.literal: His words were very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: His words were exceedingly blunt.

sentences.zh: 帝以方修省，皆不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor because he was then practicing self-cultivation and restraint punished none of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, then observing a period of self-restraint, punished none of them.

sentences.zh: 後以吏盜鬻舊賜外蕃故敕事，下綱、章吏，貶之外。

translations.literal: Later, on the matter of clerks stealing and selling old bestowed former edicts to foreign tribes, Gang and Zhang's clerks were implicated and demoted to the outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when clerks were found to have stolen and sold old imperial edicts bestowed on foreign tribes, Peng Gang and Su Zhang were implicated through their subordinates and demoted to posts abroad.

sentences.zh: 而密諭吏部尚書尹旻出旦等，且書六十人姓名於屏，俟奏遷則貶遠惡地。

translations.literal: Yet secretly he instructed Minister of Personnel Yin Min to post Dan and others out, and moreover wrote sixty men's names on a screen—when memorials for transfer were submitted they would be demoted to distant evil lands.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he secretly instructed Minister of Personnel Yin Min to post Li Dan and others out, and wrote sixty names on a screen, ordering that whenever a transfer memorial arrived those men be sent to remote and harsh posts.

sentences.zh: 旦乃與給事中盧瑀、秦昇、童同日俱謫。

translations.literal: Dan then together with supervising secretaries Lu Yu, Qin Sheng, and Tong on the same day were all banished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dan was banished on the same day as supervising secretaries Lu Yu, Qin Sheng, and Tong.

sentences.zh: 部臣見遠謫者多，有應遷者輒故遲之。

translations.literal: Personnel officials, seeing that distant banishments were many, whenever there were those who should be transferred deliberately delayed them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how many had been sent to distant posts, the personnel officials deliberately delayed transfers for those on the list.

sentences.zh: 升、軫遂得免。

translations.literal: Sheng and Zhen thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Sheng and Zhou Zhen thus escaped demotion.

sentences.zh: 崔升，字廷進，本樂安人。

translations.literal: Cui Sheng, courtesy name Tingjin, originally a man of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Sheng, courtesy name Tingjin, was originally from Le'an.

sentences.zh: 父為彰德庫大使，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father was Zhangde treasury commissioner, and so the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as Zhangde treasury commissioner, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 由工部主事改兵部。

translations.literal: From section chief of the Ministry of Works he was changed to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the Ministry of Works to the Ministry of War as section chief.

sentences.zh: 稍遷延安知府，四川參政。

translations.literal: Gradually he was transferred to prefect of Yan'an and Sichuan Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to prefect of Yan'an and vice commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 守官廉，居常服布袍，家童拾馬矢給爨。

translations.literal: In holding office he was clean; in ordinary life he wore cloth robes, and household boys gathered horse droppings to supply the cooking fire.
translations.idiomatic: He served with integrity, wore plain cloth robes in daily life, and had his servants gather horse dung for the cooking fire.

sentences.zh: 家居三十年，年八十八卒。

translations.literal: He dwelt at home thirty years and died at age eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for thirty years and died at eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子銑，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xian has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cui Xian has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 彭綱，清江人。

translations.literal: Peng Gang, a man of Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Gang was a native of Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 與蘇章、周軫、秦昇、童皆成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: Together with Su Zhang, Zhou Zhen, Qin Sheng, and Tong, he all became presented scholars in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He, Su Zhang, Zhou Zhen, Qin Sheng, and Tong all became presented scholars in the eleventh year of Chenghua (1475).

sentences.zh: 貶永寧知州，改汝州。

translations.literal: Demoted to prefect of Yongning, then changed to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Yongning, then transferred to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 鑿渠溉田數千畝。

translations.literal: He dug canals to irrigate several thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dug irrigation canals and watered several thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 再遷雲南提學副使。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Yunnan Vice Commissioner of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to vice commissioner of education in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 蘇章，余幹人。

translations.literal: Su Zhang, a man of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhang was a native of Yugan.

sentences.zh: 貶姚安通判，再遷延平知府。

translations.literal: Demoted to Yao'an subprefect, again transferred to Yanping prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to subprefect of Yao'an, he was later transferred to prefect of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 有政績。

translations.literal: He had achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He achieved solid results in office.

sentences.zh: 終浙江參政。

translations.literal: He ended as Zhejiang Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 周軫，莆田人，副使瑛從子。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen, a man of Putian, nephew of Vice Commissioner Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen, a native of Putian, was the nephew of Vice Commissioner Ying.

sentences.zh: 後進郎中，終山東運使。

translations.literal: Later advanced to bureau director, ended as Shandong transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to bureau director and ended as transport commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 李旦，字啟東，獻縣人。

translations.literal: Li Dan, courtesy name Qidong, a man of Xian county.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dan, courtesy name Qidong, was a native of Xian county.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua (1481).

sentences.zh: 貶鎮遠通判，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Demoted to Zhenyuan subprefect; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to subprefect of Zhenyuan, he died before long.

sentences.zh: 盧瑀，鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, a man of Yin county.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu was a native of Yin county.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 為刑科給事中，疏蠲淮、揚逋課十余萬，清西北勒市戰馬宿弊。

translations.literal: As penal-section supervising secretary, he memorialized to remit more than 100,000 in Huai and Yang arrears and cleared long-standing abuses in the northwest forced-market trade in war horses.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising secretary in the penal section, he memorialized to remit more than 100,000 taels of arrears in Huai and Yang and to clear long-standing abuses in the northwest forced-market trade in war horses.

sentences.zh: 嘗觸帝怒，杖之。

translations.literal: He once provoked the emperor's anger and was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: He once provoked the emperor's anger and was beaten in court.

sentences.zh: 遷工科都給事中，與昇、皆因星變陳言，獲譴。

translations.literal: Transferred to chief supervising secretary in the works section; together with Sheng and Tong he spoke on the celestial anomaly and was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to chief supervising secretary in the works section, he joined Sheng and Tong in speaking out when the stars changed and was punished.

sentences.zh: 瑀貶長沙通判，終廣平知府。

translations.literal: Yu was demoted to Changsha subprefect and ended as Guangping prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was demoted to subprefect of Changsha and ended as prefect of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 秦昇，南昌人，貶廣安州同知。

translations.literal: Qin Sheng, a man of Nanchang, demoted to Guang'an assistant prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Sheng, a native of Nanchang, was demoted to assistant prefect of Guang'an.

sentences.zh: 童，蘭溪人，貶興國州同知，終袁州知府。

translations.literal: Tong, a man of Lanxi, demoted to Xingguo assistant prefect, ended as Yuanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, a native of Lanxi, was demoted to assistant prefect of Xingguo and ended as prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，崔升以請召王恕忤旨，而工部主事王純亦以諫罷王恕被杖謫官。

translations.literal: At this time Cui Sheng, for asking that Wang Su be recalled, offended the imperial will; and Wang Chun, section chief in the Ministry of Works, also for remonstrating against Wang Su's dismissal, was beaten and banished from office.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Cui Sheng offended the throne by asking that Wang Su be recalled, and Wang Chun, a section chief in the Ministry of Works, was beaten and banished for remonstrating against Wang Su's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 純，仙居人。

translations.literal: Chun was a man of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chun was a native of Xianju.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua (1481).

sentences.zh: 貶思南推官。

translations.literal: Demoted to Sinan judicial aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to judicial aide of Sinan.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，屢遷湖廣提學僉事。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi he was repeatedly transferred to Huguang vice commissioner of education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi he rose repeatedly to vice commissioner of education in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 湯鼐，字用之，壽州人。

translations.literal: Tang Nai, courtesy name Yongzhi, a man of Shouzhou.
