translations.idiomatic: Tang Nai, courtesy name Yongzhi, was a native of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the eleventh year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢御史。

translations.literal: Appointed courier, promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier, then promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，首劾大學士萬安罔上誤國。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he first impeached Grand Secretary Wan An for deceiving the sovereign and harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne, he first impeached Grand Secretary Wan An for deceiving the sovereign and harming the state.

sentences.zh: 明日，宣至左順門。

translations.literal: The next day he was summoned and announced at the Left Gate of Compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was summoned to the Left Gate of Compliance.

sentences.zh: 中官森列，令跪。

translations.literal: Eunuchs stood in dense ranks and ordered him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs stood in dense ranks and ordered him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 鼐曰：「令鼐跪者，旨耶，抑太監意耶？」

translations.literal: Nai said: "He who orders Nai to kneel—is it an edict, or the eunuchs' wish?"
translations.idiomatic: Nai said, "He who orders Nai to kneel—is that an edict, or the eunuchs' wish?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「有旨。」

translations.literal: They said: "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 鼐始跪。

translations.literal: Only then did Nai kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Nai kneel.

sentences.zh: 及宣旨，言疏已留中。

translations.literal: When the edict was announced, it said the memorial had been kept within.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was read, it said his memorial had been kept within.

sentences.zh: 鼐大言：「臣所言國家大事，奈何留中？」

translations.literal: Nai spoke loudly: "What your servant spoke of were great matters of state—how can they be kept within?"
translations.idiomatic: Nai protested loudly: "What your servant addressed were great affairs of state—how can they be shelved?"

sentences.zh: 已而安斥，鼐亦出畿輔印馬，馳疏言：「陛下視朝之余，宜禦便殿，擇侍臣端方謹厚若劉健、謝遷、程敏政、吳寬者，日與講學論道，以為出治之本。

translations.literal: Soon Wan was expelled; Nai also went out to inspect horses in the capital region and hurried a memorial saying: "After Your Majesty holds court, you should attend the informal hall, choose upright and careful attendants such as Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Cheng Minzheng, and Wu Kuan, and daily study and discuss the Way with them as the root of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wan was dismissed. Nai was also sent to inspect horses in the capital region and hurriedly memorialized: "After holding court, Your Majesty should attend the informal hall, choose upright and careful ministers such as Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Cheng Minzheng, and Wu Kuan, and study and discuss the Way with them daily as the foundation of good governance.

sentences.zh: 至如內閣尹直、尚書李裕、都御史劉敷、侍郎黃景，奸邪無恥，或夤緣中官進用，或依附佞幸行私。

translations.literal: As for Grand Secretary Yin Zhi, Minister Li Yu, Censor-in-chief Liu Fu, and Vice Minister Huang Jing—they are wicked and shameless, some climbing in through eunuchs, some attaching to flatterers to pursue private gain.
translations.idiomatic: As for Grand Secretary Yin Zhi, Minister Li Yu, Censor-in-chief Liu Fu, and Vice Minister Huang Jing—they are wicked and shameless, some advancing through eunuch patronage, others clinging to favorites to pursue private ends.

sentences.zh: 不早驅斥，必累聖明。

translations.literal: If not soon driven out and expelled, they will surely burden Your Sagely Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not driven out soon, they will surely burden Your Majesty's rule.

sentences.zh: 司禮中官李榮、蕭敬曩為言官劾罷，尋夤緣復入。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs Li Rong and Xiao Jing were once impeached and dismissed by remonstrating officials, but soon climbed back in through patronage.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuchs Li Rong and Xiao Jing had once been impeached and dismissed by remonstrating officials, yet soon found their way back through patronage.

sentences.zh: 遂摭言官過，貶竄殆盡，致士氣委靡。

translations.literal: They then seized on remonstrators' faults and banished them nearly to extinction, causing scholarly morale to wilt.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized on the faults of remonstrating officials and banished them nearly to extinction, withering scholarly morale.

sentences.zh: 宜亟正典刑，勿為姑息。

translations.literal: They should urgently be punished by canonical law; do not be indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: They should be punished at once by proper law; do not indulge them.

sentences.zh: 諸傳奉得官者，請悉編置瘴鄉，示天下戒。

translations.literal: All supernumerary appointees who obtained office—we beg that they all be assigned to malarial regions as a warning to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: All supernumerary appointees who gained office should be posted to malarial regions as a warning to the realm.

sentences.zh: 且召致仕尚書王恕、王竑，都御史彭韶，僉事章懋等，而還建言得罪諸臣，以厲風節。」

translations.literal: Moreover recall retired ministers Wang Shu and Wang Hong, Censor-in-chief Peng Shao, Vice Commissioner Zhang Mao and others, and restore the various officials punished for offering counsel, to strengthen moral integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Recall retired ministers Wang Shu and Wang Hong, Censor-in-chief Peng Shao, Vice Commissioner Zhang Mao, and others, and restore officials punished for speaking up, to strengthen public integrity."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: A report was received in acknowledgment.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged the memorial.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年正月，鼐又劾禮部尚書周洪謨，侍郎倪嶽、張悅，南京兵部尚書馬文升，因言：「少傅劉吉，與萬安、尹直奸貪等耳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongzhi, Nai again impeached Minister of Rites Zhou Hongmo and Vice Ministers Ni Yue and Zhang Yue, Nanjing Minister of War Ma Wensheng, and moreover said: "Junior Mentor Liu Ji is the equal of Wan An and Yin Zhi in wicked greed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Hongzhi (1488), Nai again impeached Minister of Rites Zhou Hongmo, Vice Ministers Ni Yue and Zhang Yue, and Nanjing Minister of War Ma Wensheng, adding: "Junior Mentor Liu Ji is no better than Wan An and Yin Zhi in wicked greed.

sentences.zh: 安、直斥，而吉獨進官，不以為恥。

translations.literal: An and Zhi were expelled, yet Ji alone advanced in office and did not take it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: An and Zhi were dismissed, yet Ji alone kept rising and felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 請大申黜陟，明示勸懲。」

translations.literal: We beg a great enforcement of demotions and promotions, clearly showing encouragement and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that promotions and demotions be enforced broadly, with clear reward and punishment."

sentences.zh: 又劾李榮、蕭敬，而薦謫降進士李文祥為臺諫。

translations.literal: He again impeached Li Rong and Xiao Jing, and recommended the demoted presented scholar Li Wenxiang for a remonstrance post.
translations.idiomatic: He again impeached Li Rong and Xiao Jing and recommended the demoted presented scholar Li Wenxiang for a remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 尚書王恕以盛暑請輟經筵，鼐極言不可，語侵恕。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Su because of great heat asked to suspend the classics lecture; Nai strongly said it could not be done, his words encroaching on Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Wang Su asked to suspend the classics lecture because of the summer heat, Nai vehemently objected, his words bordering on insult to Su.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝更新庶政，言路大開。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor renewed common governance and the path of counsel was greatly opened.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was renewing government and the path of candid counsel lay wide open.

sentences.zh: 新進者爭，欲以功名自見。

translations.literal: Newcomers strove, wishing to make their merit and fame seen.
translations.idiomatic: New appointees strove to make their names through bold action.

sentences.zh: 封章旁午，頗傷激訐，鼐意氣尤銳。

translations.literal: Sealed memorials came in profusion, often wounding with sharp denunciation; Nai's spirit was especially keen.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials poured in, often harsh to the point of injury; Nai's tone was especially sharp.

sentences.zh: 其所抨擊，間及海內人望，以故大臣多畏之，而吉尤不能堪。

translations.literal: Those he attacked sometimes touched men of renown throughout the realm; for this reason many great ministers feared him, and Ji especially could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: His targets sometimes included men of national renown, so many senior ministers feared him, and Ji especially could not endure him.

sentences.zh: 使人啖御史魏璋曰：「君能去鼐，行僉院事矣。」

translations.literal: He sent someone to entice Censor Wei Zhang, saying: "If you can remove Nai, you will be made vice commissioner of the censorate."
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to entice Censor Wei Zhang, saying, "If you can remove Nai, you will be made vice commissioner of the censorate."

sentences.zh: 璋欣然，日夜伺鼐短。

translations.literal: Zhang gladly accepted and day and night watched for Nai's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang accepted gladly and day and night watched for faults in Nai.

sentences.zh: 未幾，而吉人之獄起。

translations.literal: Before long the case of Ji Ren arose.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the case of Ji Ren arose.

sentences.zh: 吉人者，長安人。

translations.literal: Ji Ren was a man of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ren was a native of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 成化末進士，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: A presented scholar at the end of Chenghua, he served as secretarial receptionist.
translations.idiomatic: A presented scholar at the end of Chenghua, he served as a secretarial receptionist.

sentences.zh: 四川饑，帝遣郎中江漢往振。

translations.literal: Sichuan suffered famine; the emperor sent Bureau Director Jiang Han to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan suffered famine, the emperor sent Bureau Director Jiang Han to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 人言漢不勝任，宜遣四使分道振，且擇才能御史為巡按，庶荒政有裨。

translations.literal: People said Han was not equal to the task; four envoys should be sent on separate routes to relieve, and capable censors chosen as grand coordinators, so that famine administration might be helped.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Han was unequal to the task; four envoys should relieve famine by separate routes, and capable censors should be chosen as grand coordinators so that relief might be effective.

sentences.zh: 因薦給事中宋琮、陳矞、韓鼎，御史曹璘，郎中王沂、洪鐘，員外郎東思誠，評事王寅，理刑知縣韓福及壽州知州劉概可使，而巡按則鼐足任之。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended supervising secretaries Song Cong, Chen Yu, and Han Ding, Censor Cao Lin, Bureau Directors Wang Yi and Hong Zhong, Vice Director Dong Sicheng, judicial reviewer Wang Yin, judicial magistrate Han Fu, and Shouzhou Prefect Liu Gai as fit for service, while for grand coordinator Nai alone was adequate.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended supervising secretaries Song Cong, Chen Yu, and Han Ding, Censor Cao Lin, bureau directors Wang Yi and Hong Zhong, vice director Dong Sicheng, judicial reviewer Wang Yin, judicial magistrate Han Fu, and Shouzhou prefect Liu Gai, and said Nai alone was fit to serve as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 璋遂草疏，偽署御史陳景隆等名，言吉人抵抗成命，私立朋黨。

translations.literal: Zhang then drafted a memorial, falsely signing the names of Censor Chen Jinglong and others, saying Ji Ren resisted the completed command and privately formed a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang then drafted a memorial, forging the names of Censor Chen Jinglong and others, accusing Ji Ren of resisting the imperial command and forming a private faction.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下人詔獄，令自引其黨。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sent him to the imperial prison, and ordered him to name his own faction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, sent him to the imperial prison, and ordered him to name his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 人以鼐、璘、思誠、概、福對。

translations.literal: People named Nai, Lin, Sicheng, Gai, and Fu in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Informants named Nai, Lin, Sicheng, Gai, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 璋又嗾御史陳璧等言：「璘、福、思誠非其黨，其黨則鼐、概及主事李文祥、庶吉士鄒智、知州董傑是也。

translations.literal: Zhang again instigated Censor Chen Bi and others to say: "Lin, Fu, and Sicheng are not his faction; his faction is Nai, Gai, Section Chief Li Wenxiang, Hanlin bachelor Zou Zhi, and Prefect Dong Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang then instigated Censor Chen Bi and others to say, "Lin, Fu, and Sicheng are not his faction; his faction is Nai, Gai, section chief Li Wenxiang, Hanlin bachelor Zou Zhi, and prefect Dong Jie.

sentences.zh: 概嘗饋鼐白金，貽之書，謂夜夢一人騎牛幾墮，鼐手挽之得不仆，又見鼐手執五色石引牛就道。

translations.literal: Gai once presented Nai with white silver and sent a letter saying he dreamed of a man riding an ox almost falling, Nai pulling him by hand so he did not collapse, and again seeing Nai holding a five-colored stone leading the ox onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: Gai had once given Nai silver and sent a letter saying he dreamed of a man on an ox nearly falling, Nai catching him so he did not fall, and then seeing Nai with a five-colored stone leading the ox onto the road.

sentences.zh: 因解之曰：『人騎牛謂朱，乃國姓。

translations.literal: He therefore explained it, saying: 'A man riding an ox means Zhu—it is the national surname.
translations.idiomatic: He explained: 'A man riding an ox suggests Zhu—the dynastic surname.

sentences.zh: 意者國將傾，賴鼐扶之，而引君當道也。』

translations.literal: The meaning is perhaps the state will tilt, relying on Nai to support it, and leading you onto the right road.'
translations.idiomatic: He meant the state would totter and rely on Nai to steady it, and that he was leading you onto the right path.'

sentences.zh: 鼐、概等自相標榜，詆毀時政，請並文祥、智、傑逮治。」

translations.literal: Nai, Gai, and others praised one another and slandered current policy; we beg that Wenxiang, Zhi, and Jie also be seized and punished together."
translations.idiomatic: Nai, Gai, and others had praised one another and denounced current policy; he asked that Wenxiang, Zhi, and Jie be arrested and punished as well."

sentences.zh: 疏上，吉從中主之，悉下詔獄，欲盡置之死。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, Ji backed it from within; all were sent to the imperial prison and he wished to put them all to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Ji backed it from within; all were sent to the imperial prison, and he sought to put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書何喬新、侍郎彭韶等持之，外議亦洶洶不平。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice He Qiaoxin and Vice Minister Peng Shao and others held to their view; outside opinion also surged with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice He Qiaoxin and Vice Minister Peng Shao held firm, and public opinion seethed with outrage.

sentences.zh: 乃坐概妖言律斬；

translations.literal: Gai was then sentenced under the law on heterodox speech to be beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: Gai was sentenced under the law on heterodox speech to be beheaded;

sentences.zh: 鼐受賄，戍肅州；

translations.literal: Nai accepted bribes and was banished to Suzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Nai was convicted of taking bribes and banished to Suzhou;

sentences.zh: 人欺罔，削籍；

translations.literal: Ren deceived and was struck from the registry;
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ren was convicted of deception and struck from the registry;

sentences.zh: 智、文祥、傑皆謫官。

translations.literal: Zhi, Wenxiang, and Jie were all demoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Wenxiang, and Jie were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王恕奏曰：「律重妖言，謂造作符讖類耳。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Shu memorialized, saying: "The law weighs heavily on heterodox speech, meaning the fabrication of omens and prognostications.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Shu memorialized: "The law on heterodox speech targets the fabrication of omens and prognostications.

sentences.zh: 概書詞雖妄，良以鼐數言事不避利害，因推詡之。

translations.literal: Though Gai's written words were wild, it was truly because Nai repeatedly spoke on affairs without avoiding gain or harm, and therefore he praised and flattered him.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's letter was wild, but it arose because Nai had repeatedly spoken without regard for personal risk, and Gai had praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 今當以妖言，設有如造亡秦讖者，更何以罪之？」

translations.literal: Now if he is to be charged with heterodox speech, suppose there were one who fabricated a prophecy of Qin's fall—how would he then be punished?"
translations.idiomatic: If this is heterodox speech, what charge would apply to one who forged a prophecy of Qin's fall?"

sentences.zh: 帝得疏意動，命姑繫獄。

translations.literal: The emperor, moved by the memorial, ordered them temporarily held in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the memorial, the emperor ordered them held in prison for the time being.

sentences.zh: 既而熱審，喬新等言：「概本不應妖言律。

translations.literal: Soon after, at the summer judicial review, Qiaoxin and others said: "Gai originally should not fall under the law on heterodox speech.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer judicial review, Qiaoxin and others said, "Gai should never have been charged under the law on heterodox speech.

sentences.zh: 且概五歲而孤，無兄弟，母孫氏守節三十年，曾被旌，老病且貧。

translations.literal: Moreover Gai was orphaned at five, had no brothers; his mother the Sun clan kept her chastity thirty years, was once honored, and is old, ill, and poor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Gai was orphaned at five and had no brothers; his mother of the Sun clan had kept her chastity for thirty years, had been honored by the state, and was now old, ill, and poor.

sentences.zh: 概死，母必不全，祈聖恩矜恤。」

translations.literal: If Gai dies, his mother will surely not survive whole; we pray the sage grace show pity."
translations.idiomatic: If Gai dies, his mother cannot survive; we beg imperial mercy."

sentences.zh: 乃減概死，戍海州。

translations.literal: Gai's death was then reduced and he was banished to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's death sentence was commuted and he was banished to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 槩，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Gai, a man of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gai was a native of Jining.

sentences.zh: 成化二十年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the twentieth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the twentieth year of Chenghua (1484).

sentences.zh: 除壽州知州，毀境內淫祠幾盡，三年教化大行。

translations.literal: Appointed Shouzhou prefect, he destroyed nearly all licentious shrines within the jurisdiction; in three years transformative teaching flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Shouzhou, he destroyed nearly all improper shrines in the prefecture; within three years moral instruction flourished.

sentences.zh: 弘治初上言：「刑賞予奪，人主大柄，後世乃有為女子、小人、強臣、外戚所攘竊者，由此輩心險術巧，人主稍加親信，輒墮計中。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he submitted counsel: "Punishment, reward, grant, and denial are the great handle of the sovereign; later ages have had them usurped by women, petty men, powerful ministers, and consort kin—because such people are treacherous in heart and crafty in method, and if the sovereign slightly adds trust, he at once falls into their schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he memorialized: "Punishment, reward, grant, and denial are the sovereign's great prerogatives; later ages have seen them seized by women, petty men, powerful ministers, and consort kin—because such people are treacherous and crafty, and once the ruler trusts them even slightly, he falls into their schemes.

sentences.zh: 愛者，乘君之喜而遊言以揚之；

translations.literal: Those he favors ride the ruler's joy and roam with words to exalt him;
translations.idiomatic: Those the ruler favors ride on his joy and ply him with flattering words;

sentences.zh: 惡者，乘君之怒而微言以中之，使賢人君子卒受曖昧而去。

translations.literal: those he hates ride the ruler's anger and with subtle words strike the mark, causing worthy gentlemen in the end to suffer obscurity and depart.
translations.idiomatic: those he hates ride on his anger and use subtle words to strike home, until worthy men leave office under a cloud.

sentences.zh: 卿相缺人，則遷延餌引，待有交通請屬軟美易制之人，然後薦用。

translations.literal: When ministers and chancellors lack men, they delay and bait, waiting for those with connections, requests, and patronage who are soft, compliant, and easy to control, and then recommend and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: When high offices lack appointees, they delay and bait, waiting for men with connections and patronage who are pliable and easy to control, then recommend them.

sentences.zh: 其剛正不阿者，輒媒孽而放棄之，俟其氣衰慮易，不至大立異同，乃更收錄。

translations.literal: Those upright and unbending they at once slander and cast aside; when their spirit weakens and thought eases, not reaching to great establishment of difference and agreement, they then take them back into the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The upright and unyielding they slander and cast aside, then take back only when their spirit has weakened and they no longer pose a serious challenge.

sentences.zh: 巧計既行，刑賞予奪雖名人主獨操，實一出於其所簸弄。

translations.literal: Once crafty schemes are in motion, though punishment, reward, grant, and denial are named as solely wielded by the sovereign, in truth they all issue from what they toss and manipulate.
translations.idiomatic: Once their schemes succeed, punishment and reward are said to rest with the sovereign alone, but in truth they issue from their manipulation.

sentences.zh: 迨黨立勢成，復恐一旦敗露，則又極意以排諫諍之士。

translations.literal: When the faction is established and power formed, they again fear sudden exposure, and then with utmost intent expel remonstrating scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When their faction is entrenched, fearing exposure, they do their utmost to drive out remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 務使其君孤立於上，耳無聞，目無見，以圖便其私，不至其身與國俱敗不止。

translations.literal: They strive to make their ruler isolated above, ears hearing nothing, eyes seeing nothing, to seek convenience for their private ends—not stopping until their persons and the state together fail.
translations.idiomatic: They strive to isolate the ruler above, deaf and blind, to serve their private ends, and do not stop until they and the state fall together.

sentences.zh: 故夫刑賞予奪，必由大臣奏請、臺諫集議而後可行。

translations.literal: Therefore punishment, reward, grant, and denial must go through great ministers' memorial requests and remonstrators' collective deliberation before they may be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore punishment and reward must pass through ministers' memorials and remonstrators' collective deliberation before they may be enacted.

sentences.zh: 或有矯誣，窮治不輕貸，則讒佞莫能間，而權不下移矣。」

translations.literal: If there is perverse false accusation, pursue it to the end without light pardon—then slanderers and flatterers cannot intervene, and power will not shift downward."
translations.idiomatic: If accusations are false, pursue them relentlessly; then slanderers cannot intervene and power will not slip away."

sentences.zh: 考績赴都，遂遇禍，竟卒於戍所。

translations.literal: On performance review he went to the capital, then met disaster, and in the end died at the place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the capital for his performance review he met disaster and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 鼐既戍，無援之者，久之始釋歸。

translations.literal: After Nai was banished, none aided him; only after a long time was he released to return.
translations.idiomatic: After Nai was banished, no one spoke for him; only after a long time was he released to return home.

sentences.zh: 董傑，涇縣人。

translations.literal: Dong Jie, native of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jie was a native of Jing County.

sentences.zh: 成化末進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chenghua reign, jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 鼐之論暑月輟講也，傑方謁選，亦抗疏爭，由是知名。

translations.literal: When Nai argued against suspending lectures in the summer months, Jie was just awaiting selection of his posting and also submitted a defiant memorial in protest; thereby he became well known.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Nai argued against suspending summer lectures, Jie was awaiting his official posting and likewise submitted a defiant memorial; he became well known from this.

sentences.zh: 授沔陽知州，甫數月，逮系詔獄，謫四川行都司知事，歷遷河南左布政使。

translations.literal: Appointed prefect of Mianyang; after only a few months, seized and imprisoned in the imperial prison, demoted to registrar of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, and through promotions reached Left Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Mianyang; after only a few months he was seized and held in the imperial prison, demoted to registrar of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, and eventually rose to Left Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 所在盡職業，為民所懷。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he fully fulfilled his duties and was cherished by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he fulfilled his duties fully and won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 正德六年，江西盜起，巡撫王哲兵敗召還，擢傑右副都御史代之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde, bandits rose in Jiangxi; Grand Coordinator Wang Zhe was defeated in battle and recalled; Jie was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengde bandits rose in Jiangxi; Grand Coordinator Wang Zhe was defeated and recalled, and Jie was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 璋既為吉心腹，果擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Zhang having become Ji's confidant, was indeed promoted to vice commissioner of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, having become Liu Ji's confidant, was indeed promoted to vice commissioner of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 坐事下獄，黜為九江同知，悒悒死。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was sent to prison, demoted to subprefect of Jiujiang, and died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in an offense, he was imprisoned, demoted to subprefect of Jiujiang, and died in dejection.

sentences.zh: 姜綰，字玉卿。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan, styled Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan, styled Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 弋陽人。

translations.literal: Native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 由景陵知縣擢南京御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Jingling he was promoted to Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Jingling he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，陳治道十事。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he presented ten matters for governing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he memorialized on ten matters of governance.

sentences.zh: 又言午朝宜論大政，毋泛陳細故，皆報聞。

translations.literal: He also said the midday audience should discuss great affairs of state, not broadly present minor details—all were acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the midday audience should address major policy, not minor details; the court took note.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，南京守備中官蔣琮以蘆場事下綰覆按，琮囑綰求右己。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Nanjing garrison eunuch Jiang Cong was sent down for Wan to reinvestigate on the reed-field affair; Cong asked Wan to favor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, Nanjing garrison eunuch Jiang Cong was referred to Wan for reinvestigation in the reed-field case; Cong asked Wan to rule in his favor.

sentences.zh: 綰疏言：「琮以守備重臣與小民爭利，假公事以適私情。

translations.literal: Wan memorialized: "Cong, as a garrison eunuch of heavy rank, contends for profit with common people, using public business to suit private feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Wan memorialized: "As a senior garrison eunuch, Cong contends for profit with commoners and uses public business for private ends.

sentences.zh: 用揭帖而抗詔旨，揚言陰中，脅以必從。

translations.literal: He used informal notes to resist imperial edicts, proclaimed he would strike from the shadows, and coerced by demanding compliance.
translations.idiomatic: He used informal notes to defy imperial edicts, threatened covert retaliation, and coerced others into compliance.

sentences.zh: 其他變亂成法，厥罪有十。

translations.literal: His other violations and subversions of established law—his crimes number ten.
translations.idiomatic: His other violations of law amount to ten crimes.

sentences.zh: 以內官侵言官職，罪一。

translations.literal: As an inner eunuch he encroached on the remonstrating officials' duties—crime one.
translations.idiomatic: An inner eunuch encroaching on remonstrators' duties—first crime.

sentences.zh: 妒害大臣，妄論都御史秦纮，罪二。

translations.literal: Jealous and harming great ministers, rashly criticizing Grand Coordinator Qin Hong—crime two.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous attacks on great ministers, rashly denouncing Grand Coordinator Qin Hong—second crime.

sentences.zh: 怒河閘官失迎候，欲奏罷之，罪三。

translations.literal: Angry that river-lock officials failed to greet him, he wished to memorialize to dismiss them—crime three.
translations.idiomatic: Angered that river-lock officials failed to receive him, he sought to have them dismissed—third crime.

sentences.zh: 受民詞不由通政，罪四。

translations.literal: Receiving commoners' petitions without going through the Office of Transmission—crime four.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting commoners' petitions without the Office of Transmission—fourth crime.

sentences.zh: 分遣腹心，侵漁國課，罪五。

translations.literal: Dispatching trusted agents to encroach on and plunder state revenue—crime five.
translations.idiomatic: Sending trusted agents to encroach on state revenue—fifth crime.

sentences.zh: 按季收班匠工銀，罪六。

translations.literal: Collecting by season the silver of rostered artisan labor—crime six.
translations.idiomatic: Collecting seasonal silver from rostered artisan labor—sixth crime.

sentences.zh: 擅收用罷閑都事，罪七。

translations.literal: Arrogantly employing dismissed idle secretaries—crime seven.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogantly employing dismissed idle secretaries—seventh crime.

sentences.zh: 官僚忤意，輒肆中傷，罪八。

translations.literal: When officials displeased him, he at once slandered them—crime eight.
translations.idiomatic: Slandering officials who displeased him—eighth crime.

sentences.zh: 妄奏主事周琦罪，欺罔朝廷，罪九。

translations.literal: Rashly memorializing on the crime of Director Zhou Qi, deceiving and misleading the court—crime nine.
translations.idiomatic: Falsely memorializing on Director Zhou Qi's crimes and deceiving the court—ninth crime.

sentences.zh: 保舉罷斥內臣，竊天子威柄，罪十。」

translations.literal: Recommending dismissed inner eunuchs and usurping the Son of Heaven's authority—crime ten."
translations.idiomatic: Recommending dismissed inner eunuchs and usurping the Son of Heaven's authority—tenth crime."

sentences.zh: 事下南京三法司。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Three Offices of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Three Offices of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 既，復特遣官覆治以奏。

translations.literal: Thereafter, officials were again specially dispatched to reinvestigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were then specially dispatched to reinvestigate and report.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史余濬劾中官陳祖生違制墾後湖田，湖為之淤。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor Yu Jun had impeached eunuch Chen Zu Sheng for violating regulations in reclaiming fields behind the lake, and the lake silted up from it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor Yu Jun had impeached eunuch Chen Zu Sheng for illegally reclaiming land behind the lake, which caused the lake to silt up.

sentences.zh: 奏下南京主事盧錦勘報。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to Nanjing Director Lu Jin to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to Nanjing Director Lu Jin for investigation.

sentences.zh: 錦故與祖生有隙。

translations.literal: Jin had long borne a grudge against Zu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had long borne a grudge against Zu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 而給事中方向嘗率同官繆樗等劾祖生及文武大臣不職狀，又因雷震孝陵柏，劾大學士劉吉等十一人，而詆祖生益力。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Supervising Secretary Fang Xiang had once led fellow supervising secretaries Miu Chu and others to impeach Zu Sheng and civil and military great ministers for dereliction, and because lightning struck a cypress at Xiaoling, impeached eleven men including Grand Secretary Liu Ji, denouncing Zu Sheng all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fang Xiang had led Miu Chu and others to impeach Zu Sheng and negligent ministers; he also impeached Grand Secretary Liu Ji and ten others after lightning struck a cypress at Xiaoling, denouncing Zu Sheng with particular force.

sentences.zh: 祖生銜向切骨。

translations.literal: Zu Sheng bore Xiang a mortal grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Sheng bore Xiang a mortal grudge.

sentences.zh: 時向方監後湖黃冊，祖生遂揭向、錦實侵湖田。

translations.literal: At the time Xiang was supervising the yellow register of the rear lake; Zu Sheng then exposed that Xiang and Jin had in fact encroached on lake fields.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiang was supervising the rear-lake land register, Zu Sheng exposed Xiang and Jin for encroaching on lake land.

sentences.zh: 詔下法司勘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the judicial offices to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the judicial offices to investigate.

sentences.zh: 勘未上，而琮為綰所劾。

translations.literal: Before the investigation was submitted, Cong was impeached by Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the report was filed, Cong was impeached by Wan.

sentences.zh: 於是琮、祖生及吉合謀削錦籍，謫向官，復逮綰及同官孫纮、劉遜、金章、紀傑、曹玉、譚肅、徐禮、余濬，給事中繆樗，赴京論鞫，皆謫為州判官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cong, Zu Sheng, and Ji joined in a plot to strip Jin of his registry, demote Xiang from office, and again seize Wan together with fellow censors Sun Hong, Liu Xun, Jin Zhang, Ji Ji, Cao Yu, Tan Su, Xu Li, Yu Jun, and supervising secretary Miu Chu, sending them to the capital for trial—all were demoted to assistant prefects of prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, Zu Sheng, and Ji then conspired to strip Jin of his registry, demote Xiang, and seize Wan together with fellow censors Sun Hong, Liu Xun, Jin Zhang, Ji Ji, Cao Yu, Tan Su, Xu Li, Yu Jun, and supervising secretary Miu Chu for trial at the capital; all were demoted to prefectural assistant prefects.

sentences.zh: 綰謫判桂陽，量移寧國同知，遷慶遠知府。

translations.literal: Wan was demoted to assistant prefect of Guiyang, transferred to subprefect of Ningguo, and promoted to prefect of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was demoted to assistant prefect of Guiyang, transferred to subprefect of Ningguo, and promoted to prefect of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 斬劇賊韋七旋、韋萬妙。

translations.literal: He beheaded the fierce bandits Wei Qixuan and Wei Wanmiao.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the fierce bandits Wei Qixuan and Wei Wanmiao.

sentences.zh: 其黨糾賊數萬攻城，綰堅守，檄民兵夾擊，破走之。

translations.literal: Their faction gathered tens of thousands of bandits to attack the city; Wan held firm, summoned militia to strike from both sides, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers mustered tens of thousands to attack the city; Wan held firm, called up militia to strike from both sides, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 東蘭諸州蠻悉歸侵地。

translations.literal: The Yi of the eastern Lan prefectures all returned the seized lands.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs of eastern Lan all returned the seized lands.

sentences.zh: 總督劉大夏奇其材，薦為右江兵備副使。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Liu Daxia admired his talent and recommended him as Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs of the Right River.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Daxia admired his ability and recommended him as Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs of the Right River.

sentences.zh: 思恩知府岑濬逐田州知府岑猛，綰獻策總督潘蕃。

translations.literal: Cen Jun, prefect of Si'en, drove out Cen Meng, prefect of Tianzhou; Wan offered strategy to Grand Coordinator Pan Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Si'en Prefect Cen Jun drove out Tianzhou Prefect Cen Meng; Wan offered strategy to Grand Coordinator Pan Fan.

sentences.zh: 蕃令與都指揮金堂合諸路兵大破賊，思恩平。

translations.literal: Fan ordered him to join Commander Jin Tang and troops from all routes in a great defeat of the bandits, and Si'en was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Fan ordered him to join Commander Jin Tang and allied forces in a great victory over the rebels, pacifying Si'en.

sentences.zh: 綰條二府形勢，請改設流官，比中土，廷議從之。

translations.literal: Wan set forth the strategic situation of the two prefectures and requested changing to regular officials as in the interior; court deliberation followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan outlined the situation of the two prefectures and urged appointing regular officials as in the interior; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 綰引疾還。

translations.literal: Wan cited illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wan cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 俄起河南按察使，尋復以疾歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to Surveillance Commissioner of Henan, but again returned on illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Henan, but again retired on illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 余濬，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Yu Jun, native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun was a native of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua (1481).

sentences.zh: 孝宗初，疏請永除納粟入監令。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaozong's reign he memorialized to abolish permanently the order for grain purchase entry into the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaozong's reign he memorialized to abolish permanently the purchase of grain for admission to the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 又劾浙江鎮守中官張慶、廣東鎮守中官韋眷，因薦王恕堪內閣，馬文升、彭韶、張悅、阮勤、黃孔昭堪吏部。

translations.literal: He also impeached Zhejiang garrison eunuch Zhang Qing and Guangdong garrison eunuch Wei Juan, and recommended Wang Shu as fit for the Grand Secretariat, Ma Wensheng, Peng Shao, Zhang Yue, Ruan Qin, and Huang Kongzhao as fit for the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Zhejiang garrison eunuch Zhang Qing and Guangdong garrison eunuch Wei Juan, and recommended Wang Shu for the Grand Secretariat and Ma Wensheng, Peng Shao, Zhang Yue, Ruan Qin, and Huang Kongzhao for the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 後湖之勘，自濬啟之。

translations.literal: The rear-lake investigation began with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The rear-lake investigation began with Jun.

sentences.zh: 貶平度州判官，終知府。

translations.literal: Demoted to assistant prefect of Pingdu, and ended as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to assistant prefect of Pingdu, he ended his career as prefect.

sentences.zh: 方向，字與義，桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Xiang, styled Yiyi, native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xiang, styled Yiyi, was a native of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua (1481).

sentences.zh: 謫雲南多羅驛丞，歷官瓊州知府。

translations.literal: Demoted to assistant of Duoluo courier station in Yunnan, and through offices reached prefect of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to registrar of Duoluo courier station in Yunnan, he rose to prefect of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 入覲時，仆私市一珠，索而投諸海。

translations.literal: When he came to audience, a servant privately bought a pearl; he demanded it and cast it into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting himself at court, a servant privately bought a pearl; he seized it and threw it into the sea.

sentences.zh: 繆樗，字全之，溧陽人。

translations.literal: Miu Chu, styled Quanzhi, native of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Miu Chu, styled Quanzhi, was a native of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the eleventh year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初，陳時政八事。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaozong's reign he presented eight matters of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaozong's reign he presented eight matters of current policy.

sentences.zh: 因劾大學士尹直等，時號「敢言」。

translations.literal: He thereby impeached Grand Secretary Yin Zhi and others, and at the time was called "daring in speech."
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Grand Secretary Yin Zhi and others, and was known at the time as "daring in speech."

sentences.zh: 終營州判官。

translations.literal: He ended as assistant prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as assistant prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孫纮，字文冕，鄞人。

translations.literal: Sun Hong, styled Wenmian, native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hong, styled Wenmian, was a native of Yin county.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 謫膠州判官，遷廣德知州，卒官。

translations.literal: Demoted to assistant prefect of Jiaozhou, transferred to magistrate of Guangde, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to assistant prefect of Jiaozhou, he was transferred to magistrate of Guangde and died in office.

sentences.zh: 纮少貧，傭書市肉以養母。

translations.literal: Hong was poor in youth, hiring out to copy books to buy meat to nourish his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was poor in youth and hired out as a copyist to buy meat to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 既通籍，終身不食肉。

translations.literal: Once entered the registers, he never ate meat for life.
translations.idiomatic: After entering official service he never ate meat for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 劉遜，安福人。

translations.literal: Liu Xun, native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun was a native of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 謫澧州判官，遷武岡知州。

translations.literal: Demoted to assistant prefect of Li, transferred to magistrate of Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to assistant prefect of Li, he was transferred to magistrate of Wugang.

sentences.zh: 岷王不檢下，遜裁抑之，又欲損其歲祿。

translations.literal: The Prince of Min was undisciplined with subordinates; Xun restrained him and also wished to reduce his annual stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Min did not restrain his household; Xun curbed them and also sought to reduce his annual stipend.

sentences.zh: 王怒，奏於朝，征下詔獄，貶四川行都司斷事，歷湖廣副使。

translations.literal: The prince was angry and memorialized to the court; summoned and sent to the imperial prison, demoted to judicial officer of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, and through offices reached Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was angered and memorialized to the court; Xun was summoned to the imperial prison, demoted to judicial officer of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, and later rose to Vice Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾征賄不得，坐缺軍儲被逮，已而釋之。

translations.literal: Liu Jin sought bribes and did not obtain them; on the charge of shortfall in military provisions he was seized, then soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin demanded bribes and received none; on a charge of shortfall in military provisions Xun was seized, then soon released.

sentences.zh: 再坐斷獄稽延，罰米百石。

translations.literal: Again on the charge of delay in judging cases, fined one hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for delay in judging cases, he was fined one hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 先是，榮王乞辰州、常德田二千頃、山場八百里、民舍市廛千余間，遜與巡撫韓重持勿予。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Rong had requested two thousand qing of fields in Chenzhou and Changde, eight hundred li of mountain estates, and more than a thousand commoners' dwellings and market stalls; Xun and Grand Coordinator Han Chong firmly withheld granting them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Rong had requested two thousand qing of Chenzhou and Changde fields, eight hundred li of mountain estates, and more than a thousand dwellings and market stalls; Xun and Grand Coordinator Han Chong firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，瑾悉予之。

translations.literal: At this time Jin granted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jin granted them all.

sentences.zh: 部議補遜瓊州副使，瑾勒令致仕。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated appointing Xun Vice Commissioner of Qiongzhou; Jin forced him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry proposed appointing Xun Vice Commissioner of Qiongzhou; Jin forced him to retire.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起官，歷福建按察使。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was recalled to office and served as Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Xun was recalled and served as Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 金章等無他表見。

translations.literal: Jin Zhang and the others showed nothing else of note.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhang and the others left no further record of distinction.

sentences.zh: 姜洪，字希範，廣德人。

translations.literal: Jiang Hong, styled Xifan, native of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Hong, styled Xifan, was a native of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 除盧氏知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lushi.

sentences.zh: 單騎勸農桑。

translations.literal: He rode alone to encourage agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone to encourage farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 民姜仲禮願代父死罪，洪奏免之。

translations.literal: A commoner, Jiang Zhongli, wished to die in his father's stead; Hong memorialized to exempt him.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Jiang Zhongli offered to die in his father's place; Hong memorialized to spare the father.

sentences.zh: 征拜御史。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，陳時政八事。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, Hong set forth eight matters of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Jiang Hong set forth eight matters of current policy.

sentences.zh: 歷詆太監蕭敬，內閣萬安、劉吉，學士尹直，侍郎黃景、劉宣，都御史劉敷，尚書李裕、李敏、杜銘，大理丞宋經，而薦致仕尚書王恕、王竑、李秉，去任侍郎謝鐸，編修張元禎，檢討陳獻章，僉事章懋，評事黃仲昭，御史強珍、徐鏞、於大節，給事中王徽、蕭顯、賀欽，員外林俊，主事王純及現任尚書余子俊、馬文升，巡撫彭韶，侍郎張悅，詹事楊守陳。

translations.literal: He denounced in turn the eunuch Xiao Jing, Grand Secretaries Wan An and Liu Ji, Academician Yin Zhi, Vice Ministers Huang Jing and Liu Xuan, Censor-in-chief Liu Fu, Ministers Li Yu, Li Min, and Du Ming, and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Song Jing; and recommended retired Ministers Wang Shu, Wang Hong, and Li Bing, former Vice Minister Xie Duo, Compiler Zhang Yuanzhen, Reviser Chen Xianzhang, Intendant Zhang Mao, Review Official Huang Zhongzhao, Censors Qiang Zhen, Xu Yong, and Yu Dajie, Supervising Secretaries Wang Hui, Xiao Xian, and He Qin, Section Director Lin Jun, Section Chief Wang Chun, and the incumbent Ministers Yu Zijun and Ma Wensheng, Grand Coordinator Peng Shao, Vice Minister Zhang Yue, and Grand Mentor Yang Shouchen.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced in turn the eunuch Xiao Jing, Grand Secretaries Wan An and Liu Ji, Academician Yin Zhi, Vice Ministers Huang Jing and Liu Xuan, Censor-in-chief Liu Fu, Ministers Li Yu, Li Min, and Du Ming, and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Song Jing, while recommending retired Ministers Wang Shu, Wang Hong, and Li Bing, former Vice Minister Xie Duo, Compiler Zhang Yuanzhen, Reviser Chen Xianzhang, Intendant Zhang Mao, Review Official Huang Zhongzhao, Censors Qiang Zhen, Xu Yong, and Yu Dajie, Supervising Secretaries Wang Hui, Xiao Xian, and He Qin, Section Director Lin Jun, Section Chief Wang Chun, and the incumbent Ministers Yu Zijun and Ma Wensheng, Grand Coordinator Peng Shao, Vice Minister Zhang Yue, and Grand Mentor Yang Shouchen.

sentences.zh: 且言指揮許寧、內官懷恩，並拔出曹輩，足副任使。

translations.literal: He also said that Commander Xu Ning and the eunuch Huai En, together with removing Cao's faction, were fully adequate to their appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Commander Xu Ning and the eunuch Huai En, once Cao's faction was removed, were fully adequate to their duties.

sentences.zh: 他所陳，多斥近幸，疏辭幾萬言。

translations.literal: What else he set forth mostly denounced those near and favored; the memorial ran to nearly ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Much of what he set forth denounced imperial favorites, and the memorial ran to nearly ten thousand words.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 為所斥者憾不置。

translations.literal: Those he had denounced harbored resentment without end.
translations.idiomatic: Those he had denounced nursed endless resentment.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，出按湖廣，與督漕都御史秦纮爭文移，被劾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he went out to inspect Huguang and quarreled over documents with Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Qin Hong; he was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi (1488) he went out to inspect Huguang and quarreled over official correspondence with Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Qin Hong, and was impeached.

sentences.zh: 所司白洪無罪。

translations.literal: The responsible office reported that Hong was not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office reported that Hong was innocent.

sentences.zh: 劉吉欲中之，再下禮部會議，遂貶夏縣知縣。

translations.literal: Liu Ji wished to strike at him; the matter was twice sent down to the Ministry of Rites for joint deliberation, and Hong was demoted to magistrate of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji sought to bring him down; the case was twice referred to the Ministry of Rites for joint deliberation, and Hong was demoted to magistrate of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 御史歐陽旦請召還洪及暢亨等，不納。

translations.literal: Censor Ouyang Dan asked that Hong and Chang Heng and others be recalled; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ouyang Dan asked that Hong and Chang Heng and others be recalled, but the court would not agree.

sentences.zh: 遷桂林知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Guilin.

sentences.zh: 瑤、僮侵擾古田，請兵討平之，擢雲南參政。

translations.literal: When Yao and Zhuang raided Gutian, he requested troops to suppress them and was promoted to Yunnan administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao and Zhuang peoples raided Gutian, he requested troops to suppress them and was promoted to administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 土官陶洪與八百媳婦約為亂，洪乘間翦滅。

translations.literal: The native official Tao Hong plotted rebellion with the Lady of Baibu; Hong seized the opportunity and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: The native official Tao Hong plotted rebellion with the Lady of Baibu; Jiang Hong seized the opportunity and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 歷山東左參政。

translations.literal: He served as left administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 正德二年遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was transferred to administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde (1507) he was transferred to administration commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾索賀印錢，不應。

translations.literal: Liu Jin demanded congratulatory seal money; he did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin demanded congratulatory seal money, and he refused.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，中旨令致仕。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year an imperial rescript ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year an imperial rescript ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起山東左布政使。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was recalled as left administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, he was recalled as left administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七年以右副都御史巡撫山西，未滿歲卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi; before a year had passed he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi; he died before a year had passed.

sentences.zh: 洪性廉直，身後喪不能舉。

translations.literal: Hong's nature was upright and incorrupt; after death his family could not afford the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was upright by nature; after his death his family could not afford his funeral.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚莊介。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously honored with the epithet Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 歐陽旦，安福人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Dan, native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Dan was a native of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the seventeenth year of Chenghua (1481).

sentences.zh: 由休寧知縣擢御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Xiuning he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Xiuning he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗請逐劉吉，罷皇莊。

translations.literal: He once requested expelling Liu Ji and abolishing imperial estates.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized to expel Liu Ji and abolish imperial estates.

sentences.zh: 歷湖廣僉事、浙江副使，終南京右副都御史。

translations.literal: He served as Huguang intendant, Zhejiang vice commissioner, and ended as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Huguang intendant and Zhejiang vice commissioner, and ended as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 暢亨，字文通，河津人。

translations.literal: Chang Heng, styled Wentong, native of Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Heng, styled Wentong, was a native of Hejin.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 由長垣知縣擢御史，巡按浙江。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Changyuan he was promoted to censor and toured and inspected Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Changyuan he was promoted to censor and sent to tour and inspect Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奏罷上供綾紗等物。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he memorialized to abolish tribute deliveries of silk gauze and the like.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he memorialized to abolish tribute deliveries of silk gauze and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年二月，景寧縣屏風山異獸萬餘，大如羊，白色，銜尾浮空去。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Hongzhi, at Pingfeng Mountain in Jingning County more than ten thousand strange beasts, large as sheep and white, floated away through the air biting one another's tails.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Hongzhi (1488), at Pingfeng Mountain in Jingning County more than ten thousand strange beasts, as large as sheep and white in color, floated away through the air biting one another's tails.

sentences.zh: 亨請罷溫、處銀課，而置鎮守中官張慶於法。

translations.literal: Heng asked to abolish the silver levy in Wen and Chu and to bring the garrison eunuch Zhang Qing to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Heng asked to abolish the silver levy in Wenzhou and Chuzhou and to bring the garrison eunuch Zhang Qing to justice.

sentences.zh: 章下所司，銀課得減，責慶陳狀。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices; the silver levy was reduced, and Qing was ordered to submit a statement.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the responsible offices; the silver levy was reduced, and Zhang Qing was ordered to submit a statement.

sentences.zh: 慶因訐亨考察不公，停亨俸三月。

translations.literal: Qing therefore denounced Heng for unfair evaluation and Heng's salary was suspended for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qing denounced Heng for unfair evaluation, and Heng's salary was suspended for three months.

sentences.zh: 亨又劾僉事鄒滂，滂亦訐亨。

translations.literal: Heng again impeached Intendant Zou Pang, and Pang also denounced Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Heng again impeached Intendant Zou Pang, and Pang denounced Heng in turn.

sentences.zh: 慶等構之，逮亨，謫涇陽知縣。

translations.literal: Qing and others framed him; Heng was arrested and demoted to magistrate of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qing and others framed him; Heng was arrested and demoted to magistrate of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 給事中龐泮上疏爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Pang Pan submitted a memorial in protest; the court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Pang Pan submitted a memorial in protest, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 曹璘，字廷暉，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Cao Lin, styled Tinghui, native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Lin, styled Tinghui, was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478).

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: Appointed liturgical attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed liturgical attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，選授御史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was selected and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was selected and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，疏言：「梓宮發引，陛下宜衰绖杖履送至大明門外，拜哭而別，率宮中行三年喪。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he memorialized: "When the spirit coffin is conveyed forth, Your Majesty should go in mourning dress with staff and shoes to escort it to outside the Great Bright Gate, bow and weep in parting, and lead the palace in observing three years of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he memorialized: "When the imperial coffin is borne forth, Your Majesty should go in mourning garb, staff in hand, and escort it to beyond the Great Bright Gate, bow and weep in farewell, and lead the palace in three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 貴妃萬氏有罪，宜告於先帝，削其謚，遷葬他所。」

translations.literal: The honored consort of the Wan clan is guilty; it is fitting to report this to the Former Emperor, strip her posthumous title, and relocate her burial elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: The honored consort of the Wan clan is guilty; she should be reported to the Former Emperor, stripped of her posthumous title, and reburied elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 帝納其奏，而戒勿言貴妃事。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his memorial but admonished him not to speak of the consort matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his memorial but warned him not to raise the matter of the consort.

sentences.zh: 頃之，請進用王恕等諸大臣，復先朝言事於大節等諸臣官，放遣宮中怨女，罷撤監督京營及鎮守四方太監。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he requested promoting Wang Shu and other great ministers, restoring officials of the former court who had spoken on great matters of principle, releasing resentful women in the palace, and abolishing supervising eunuchs of the capital army and eunuchs garrisoning the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked that Wang Shu and other leading ministers be promoted, that officials of the former reign who had spoken on matters of great principle be restored, that resentful women in the palace be released, and that eunuchs supervising the capital army and garrisoning the regions be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「梁芳以指揮袁輅獻地建寺，請令襲廣平侯爵。

translations.literal: He also said: "Liang Fang, through Commander Yuan Lu, presented land to build a temple and requested that he inherit the marquisate of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Liang Fang had Commander Yuan Lu present land to build a temple and asked that Yuan inherit the marquisate of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 以數畝地得侯，勛臣誰不解體，宜亟為革罷。」

translations.literal: To obtain a marquisate for a few mu of land—which meritorious minister would not be utterly disheartened? This should urgently be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: To gain a marquisate for a few mu of land—what meritorious minister would not be utterly dismayed? This should be abolished at once."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝頗采焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor largely adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor largely adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年七月上言：「近日星隕地震，金木二星晝現，雷擊禁門，皇陵雨雹，南京內園災，狂夫叫閽，景寧白氣飛騰，而陛下不深求致咎之由，以盡弭災之實。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Hongzhi he memorialized: "Recently stars have fallen, the earth quaked, the metal and wood planets appeared by day, lightning struck the forbidden gate, hail fell at the imperial tombs, fire broke out in the inner gardens at Nanjing, a madman cried at the palace gate, white vapor soared aloft at Jingning—but Your Majesty does not deeply seek the causes of these faults in order fully to quell the substance of these calamities.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Hongzhi he memorialized: "Recently stars have fallen, the earth has quaked, the metal and wood planets have appeared by day, lightning has struck the forbidden gate, hail has fallen at the imperial tombs, fire has broken out in the inner gardens at Nanjing, a madman has cried at the palace gate, and white vapor has soared over Jingning—yet Your Majesty does not deeply investigate the causes of these faults in order fully to dispel these calamities.

sentences.zh: 經筵雖禦，徒為具文。

translations.literal: Although the lecture sessions are held, they are mere empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Although the lecture sessions are convened, they are mere empty formality.

sentences.zh: 方舉輒休，暫行遽罷，所謂『一日暴之，十日寒之』者。

translations.literal: Just when begun they are stopped; briefly carried out then hastily ended—the so-called "one day of sun, ten days of cold."
translations.idiomatic: They are begun only to be suspended, carried out briefly and then hastily abandoned—the very "one day of sun, ten days of cold" of the proverb.

sentences.zh: 願日禦講殿與儒臣論議，罷斥大學士劉吉等，以消天變。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty daily to attend the lecture hall and discuss with Confucian ministers, dismiss Grand Secretary Liu Ji and others, in order to dispel heaven's warnings.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty daily attend the lecture hall and debate with Confucian ministers, and dismiss Grand Secretary Liu Ji and others, so as to dispel heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 臣昨冬曾請陛下墨衰視政，今每遘節序，輒漸禦黃袞，從官朱緋。

translations.literal: Last winter your servant once asked Your Majesty to handle government affairs in ink-black mourning dress; now at every seasonal festival Your Majesty gradually resumes the yellow dragon robe, and attendants wear vermillion.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter your servant asked Your Majesty to conduct government in ink-black mourning dress; now at every seasonal occasion Your Majesty gradually resumes the yellow dragon robe, and attendants wear vermillion.

sentences.zh: 三年之間，為日有幾，宜但禦淺服。

translations.literal: Within the three-year period, how many days are there? Your Majesty should only wear light mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Within the three-year mourning period, how many days are there? Your Majesty should wear only light mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 且陛下方諒陰，少監郭鏞乃請選妃嬪。

translations.literal: Moreover, while Your Majesty is still in the mourning period of seclusion, Junior Eunuch Guo Yong nevertheless requested selecting consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, while Your Majesty is still observing the mourning seclusion, Junior Eunuch Guo Yong nevertheless requested that consorts be selected.

sentences.zh: 雖拒勿納，鏞猶任用，何以解臣民疑。

translations.literal: Although this was refused and not accepted, Yong is still employed—how can subjects' doubts be resolved?
translations.idiomatic: Although this was refused, Yong is still in office—how can the doubts of officials and people be dispelled?

sentences.zh: 祖宗嚴自宮之禁，今此曹幹進紛紜，當論罪。

translations.literal: The ancestors strictly prohibited interference with the inner palace; now this lot clamor for advancement in confusion—they should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors strictly forbade meddling with the inner palace; now this crowd clamor for advancement in disorder—they should be punished.

sentences.zh: 朝廷特設書堂，令翰林官教習內使，本非高皇帝制。

translations.literal: The court specially established a lecture hall, ordering Hanlin officials to instruct inner eunuchs—this was originally not the system of the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially established a lecture hall and ordered Hanlin officials to instruct inner eunuchs—this was never the High Emperor's institution.

sentences.zh: 詞臣多夤緣以幹進，而內官亦且假儒術以文奸，宜速罷之。

translations.literal: Literary officials mostly use connections to seek advancement, while inner officials also borrow Confucian learning to cloak wickedness—they should quickly be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Literary officials mostly use connections to advance themselves, while inner officials also borrow Confucian learning to cloak their wickedness—the practice should be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 諸邊有警，輒命京軍北征，此輩驕惰久，不足用。

translations.literal: When the frontiers have alarms, [the court] immediately orders capital troops north on campaign; this lot have long been arrogant and lazy and are not fit for use.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontiers are alarmed, the court immediately orders capital troops north on campaign; this corps have long been arrogant and indolent and are not fit for service.

sentences.zh: 乞自今勿遣，而以出師之費賞邊軍。」

translations.literal: I beg from now on not to dispatch them, but rather use the expenses of sending troops to reward frontier soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that from now on they not be dispatched, and that the cost of campaigns be used instead to reward frontier troops."

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，不喜，降旨譙讓。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial he was displeased and issued an edict of reproof.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the memorial he was displeased and issued an edict reproaching him.

sentences.zh: 已，出按廣東，訪陳獻章於新會，服其言論，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Thereafter he went out to inspect Guangdong, visited Chen Xianzhang at Xinhui, was convinced by his discourse, and then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he toured Guangdong as investigating censor, visited Chen Xianzhang at Xinhui, was persuaded by his teaching, and then pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 居山中讀書，三十年不入城市。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the mountains reading books and for thirty years did not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the mountains reading books and for thirty years never entered the city.

sentences.zh: 彭程，字萬里，鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Peng Cheng, styled Wanli, native of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Cheng, styled Wanli, was a native of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 成化末進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chenghua reign, jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，授御史，巡視京城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was appointed censor and inspected the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was appointed censor and toured the capital region.

sentences.zh: 降人雜處畿甸多為盜，事發則投戚裏、奄豎為窟穴。

translations.literal: Surrendered peoples mixed in the metropolitan area mostly became bandits; when matters broke out they would take refuge with imperial in-laws and eunuchs as dens.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered peoples scattered through the capital region mostly turned to banditry; when cases arose they would flee to imperial in-laws and eunuchs for shelter.

sentences.zh: 程每先機制之，有發輒得。

translations.literal: Cheng each time seized the initiative and controlled them; whenever outbreaks occurred he apprehended them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng each time anticipated them and checked them; whenever trouble broke out he caught the culprits.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽兩浙，代還，巡視光祿。

translations.literal: He inspected the salt administration in the two Zhe provinces; when replaced and returned, he inspected the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the salt administration in the two Zhe provinces; when relieved and returned, he inspected the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 五年上疏言：「臣適見光祿造皇壇器。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized: "Your servant has just seen the Court of Imperial Entertainments making utensils for the Imperial Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he memorialized: "Your servant has just seen the Court of Imperial Entertainments making vessels for the Imperial Altar.

sentences.zh: 皇壇者，先帝修齋行法之所。

translations.literal: The Imperial Altar was where the Former Emperor practiced fasting and performed ritual methods.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Altar was where the Former Emperor practiced fasting and performed ritual methods.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，此類廢斥盡，何復有皇壇煩置器？

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, such things have all been abolished and discarded—why again trouble to furnish utensils for the Imperial Altar?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, such things have all been abolished—why again trouble to supply vessels for the Imperial Altar?

sentences.zh: 光祿金錢，悉民膏血。

translations.literal: The funds of the Court of Imperial Entertainments are entirely the people's vital essence and blood.
translations.idiomatic: The funds of the Court of Imperial Entertainments are entirely the people's lifeblood.

sentences.zh: 用得其當，猶恐病民，況投之無用地。

translations.literal: Even when used appropriately one still fears harming the people—how much more when spent on useless ground.
translations.idiomatic: Even when spent appropriately one still fears burdening the people—how much more when it is poured into useless projects.

sentences.zh: 頃李孜省、繼曉輩倡邪說，而先帝篤信之者，意在遠希福壽也。

translations.literal: Recently Li Zisheng, Jixiao, and their sort spread heterodox doctrines, and what the Former Emperor deeply trusted in them aimed to was far to seek blessings and long life.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Li Zisheng, Jixiao, and their sort preached heterodox doctrines, and what the Former Emperor deeply trusted them for was to seek distant blessings and long life.

sentences.zh: 今二人已伏重辟，則禍患之來，二人尚不能自免，豈能福壽他人。

translations.literal: Now the two men have already suffered heavy punishment; then as calamities come, the two men still could not save themselves—how could they bless and lengthen the lives of others?
translations.idiomatic: Now the two men have already suffered capital punishment; if calamity comes, they could not even save themselves—how could they bring blessings and long life to others?

sentences.zh: 倘陛下果有此舉。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty indeed has such an intent.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty indeed intends this.

sentences.zh: 宜遏之將萌。

translations.literal: It should be stopped at the sprouting stage.
translations.idiomatic: It should be stopped while still in bud.

sentences.zh: 如無，請治所司逢迎罪。」

translations.literal: If not, please punish the relevant office for currying favor."
translations.idiomatic: If not, please punish the responsible officials for currying favor."

sentences.zh: 帝初無皇壇造器之命，特光祿姑為備。

translations.literal: At first the emperor had no order to make Imperial Altar utensils—it was merely the Court of Imperial Entertainments making provision in advance.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had issued no order to make Imperial Altar vessels—the Court of Imperial Entertainments was merely preparing in advance.

sentences.zh: 帝得程奏大怒，以為暴揚先帝過，立下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: When the emperor received Cheng's memorial he was furious, considering it publicly exposing the Former Emperor's faults, and immediately had him placed in the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received Cheng's memorial he was furious, regarding it as publicly exposing the Former Emperor's faults, and immediately had him imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 給事中叢蘭亦巡視光祿，繼上疏論之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Cong Lan was also inspecting the Court of Imperial Entertainments and subsequently submitted a memorial arguing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Cong Lan was also inspecting the Court of Imperial Entertainments and subsequently memorialized on the same matter.

sentences.zh: 帝宥蘭，奪光祿卿胡恭等俸，付程刑部定罪。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Lan, stripped the salaries of Court of Imperial Entertainments Director Hu Gong and others, and handed Cheng over to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Lan, stripped the salaries of Court of Imperial Entertainments Director Hu Gong and others, and handed Cheng over to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 尚書彭韶等擬贖杖還職。

translations.literal: Minister Peng Shao and others proposed redemption by fine and beating and return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Peng Shao and others proposed fine and beating in lieu of punishment and return to office.

sentences.zh: 帝欲置之死，命系之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to put him to death and ordered him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to put him to death and ordered him held in prison.

sentences.zh: 韶等復疏救，程子尚三上章乞代父死，終不聽。

translations.literal: Shao and others again memorialized to save him; Cheng's son Shang three times submitted memorials begging to die in his father's place—the emperor ultimately would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and others again memorialized to save him; Cheng's son Shang three times submitted memorials begging to die in his father's stead—the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 是時巡按陜西御史嵩縣李興亦坐酷刑系獄。

translations.literal: At this time Li Xing of Song County, touring censor of Shaanxi, was also imprisoned for cruel torture.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Xing of Song County, the touring censor of Shaanxi, was also imprisoned for cruel torture.

sentences.zh: 及朝審，上興及程罪狀。

translations.literal: At the court review the charges of Xing and Cheng were presented.
translations.idiomatic: At the court review the charges against Xing and Cheng were presented.

sentences.zh: 詔興斬，程及家屬戍隆慶。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xing beheaded; Cheng and his family were exiled to Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Xing beheaded; Cheng and his family were exiled to Longqing.

sentences.zh: 文武大臣英國公張懋等合疏言：「興所斃多罪犯，不宜當以死。

translations.literal: Civil and military great ministers including Duke of Ying Zhang Mao jointly memorialized: "Of those whom Xing put to death, many were criminals—he ought not to be punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military great ministers including the Duke of Ying, Zhang Mao, jointly memorialized: "Of those whom Xing put to death, many were criminals—he should not be punished with death.

sentences.zh: 程用諫為職，坐此戍邊，則作奸枉法者何以處之？」

translations.literal: Cheng performed remonstrance as his duty; to exile him to the frontier for this—then how are those who commit wickedness and pervert the law to be dealt with?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng performed remonstrance as his duty; to exile him to the frontier for this—then how are those who commit wickedness and pervert the law to be punished?"

sentences.zh: 尚書王恕又特疏救。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Shu again specially memorialized to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Shu again submitted a special memorial to save him.

sentences.zh: 乃減興死，杖之百，偕妻子戍賓州，程竟無所減。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xing's death was reduced; he was beaten one hundred strokes and exiled with wife and children to Binzhou; Cheng ultimately had no reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xing's death sentence was commuted; he was beaten one hundred strokes and exiled with wife and children to Binzhou; Cheng received no reduction at all.

sentences.zh: 程母李氏年老無他子，叩闕乞留侍養。

translations.literal: Cheng's mother Lady Li was old and had no other sons; she knocked at the palace gate begging to be allowed to remain and serve him in nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's mother, Lady Li, was elderly and had no other sons; she knocked at the palace gate begging to be allowed to stay and care for him.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中毛呈等亦奏曰：「昔劉禹錫附王叔文當竄遠方，裴度以其母老為請，得改連州。

translations.literal: Nanjing supervising secretaries including Mao Cheng also memorialized: "Formerly Liu Yuxi attached to Wang Shuwen was to be banished to a distant region; Pei Du pleaded that his mother was old, and he was changed to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing supervising secretaries including Mao Cheng also memorialized: "Formerly Liu Yuxi, for attaching himself to Wang Shuwen, was to be banished to a distant region; Pei Du pleaded that his mother was old, and he was reassigned to Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德，非唐中主可比，而程罪亦異禹錫。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely virtue cannot be compared to middling Tang rulers—and Cheng's offense is also unlike Liu Yuxi's.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sagely virtue cannot be compared with middling Tang rulers—and Cheng's offense is unlike Liu Yuxi's.

sentences.zh: 祈少矜憐，全其母子。」

translations.literal: I pray a little compassion and pity to preserve mother and son intact."
translations.idiomatic: I pray for a little compassion to preserve mother and son together."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: [The emperor] did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 子尚隨父戍所，遂舉廣西鄉試。

translations.literal: His son Shang followed his father to the place of exile and then passed the Guangxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shang followed his father into exile and then passed the Guangxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝念程母老，放還。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor, mindful that Cheng's mother was old, released her to return.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor, mindful that Cheng's mother was elderly, allowed her to return.

sentences.zh: 其後，劉瑾亂政，追論程巡鹽時稍虧額課，勒其家償。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Jin disturbed government, he retrospectively charged that when Cheng inspected salt he had slightly reduced the quota revenue and compelled his family to compensate.
